He simply replied to her demand with another massive array of hundreds of ice spears, which she destroyed again in one sweeping wave of her burning sword.
FWOOSH!
CRASH!
This time, he received loud boos from the disappointed audience.
"BOOOO!
VEL SIKARA!"
"BOOOO!
VEL SIKARA!"
"BOOOO!
VEL SIKARA!"
I can feel the audience really doesn’t like me fighting like this.
But I don’t give a shit.
I’m here to win and survive by any means possible, not to put on a show.
One strategic thing he was acutely aware of: his natural rate of mana recovery was literally tens of times faster than hers, based on what he could observe.
He just had to make her continuously spend her energy defending, and eventually, he would win through attrition.

chapters.title: Chapter 358: Fighting a Sage—4
paragraphs: Victory is now looking genuinely within my sight. I just need patience.
She shouted the same demand again, gesturing aggressively for him to descend.
"DEL KRESH! TOR!"
But Leon just continued his relentless ice spear bombardment, ignoring her completely.
However, just then, she stopped shouting and instead tilted her head—wistelled hard for something, as if she had lost her mind.
Why did she stop? What is she wiste—?
Leon was genuinely confused as to why she’d suddenly pause like that in the middle of active combat.

Then, just at that moment, he detected something absolutely terrifying approaching rapidly from directly behind him, because of his kilometer-wide spatial awareness spread around him since the start of the fight.
WHOOOOSH!
He felt something behind him exhale—no sound, just a furnace-hot gust of wind brushing his neck like a breath from hell.
His enhanced eyes barely caught a glimpse of a blazing ray of concentrated fire shooting toward his back at incredible speed.
SHIT!
Leon quickly teleported sideways to dodge—
FWOOSH!

Even though the attack didn’t directly touch him, the sheer ambient temperature of it passing nearby had burned and blistered the exposed tissue of his hands and face. His body, protected by his invisible armor and defensive layers, remained intact. The burns healed almost instantly due to his natural regeneration.
SIZZLE... HEAL...
However, what was truly terrifying wasn’t the attack itself—it was what had launched it.
A massive red creature—completely featureless as if constructed from solid burning metal, rough and angular—was now diving toward him.
The air around him turned acrid, thick with the reek of scorched metal and sulfur, as if the sky itself was burning.
It was many times larger than the flying mount he’d traveled on with Crimson earlier.
And it was fast. Much, much faster than that docile creature.
SCREECH! WHOOOOSH!
The thing was coming directly at him with clear hostile intent, wanting to tear him apart violently.
This has to be cheating! How is this even allowed?!
Leon looked around frantically toward the top step of the arena, seeking the monstrous man who was ultimately responsible for him being in this desperate position.
However, the man was just calmly watching with no visible reaction whatsoever. And the audience was producing thunderous cheers of excitement.
"KRESH! MANDOR! VEL SIKARA!"
Are they enjoying this? They think this is entertainment?!
Leon had no choice but to run as that enormous creature felt completely out of his league.
If that previous fire beam attack had actually connected directly, I would have been instantly erased by the sheer intensity of its power. It’s absolutely terrifying!

The flying beast’s speed—which made it look like a prehistoric dinosaur crossed with a dragon, all red scales and jagged edges with flames constantly wreathing its body—was faster than Leon could properly track with his eyes alone.
Wherever it flew, the air shimmered with heatwaves. Even a hundred meters away, Leon’s exposed skin prickled like it was being cooked.
SCREECH! FWOOSH!
Just to escape and survive, Leon had to use a desperate combination of continuous teleportation and maximum-speed flight, putting his complete focus on evasion.
The creature’s wingbeats slammed against the air like war drums, each thunderous flap echoing across the sky.
FWOOSH! FWOOSH! FWOOSH!

He didn’t even bother trying to maintain his illusion anymore, as maintaining invisibility required concentration he couldn’t spare. He needed every bit of focus just to avoid being caught in this terrifying creature’s grasp.
Can’t think about attacking the woman below anymore. Just survive! Just don’t die!

It became like a deadly game of cat and mouse in the red sky—but an extremely lethal version. They appeared like two shooting stars: one massive, red, and terrifying; another smaller, bright, and desperately flickering.
Leon was barely able to escape its conscious, calculated attacks even with his full concentration focused entirely on evasion.
SCREECH! WHOOSH! FWOOSH!
This made him internally cry out in frustration and despair.
How is this even allowed?! This is completely unfair!

He’d genuinely had hope of winning against the woman through his admittedly cheap tactics, but now she wouldn’t be getting tired anymore since he’d stopped attacking. Meanwhile, he had to dedicate his full focus to this creature’s deadly pursuit just to survive.
This is a rigged slaughter, not a fight!
And worse, soon his Rank 8 temporary affinity boost from Elemental Surge would expire and drop back to Rank 7.
When that happens, my power level will have a massive drop. I’ll be completely in this creature’s grasp. I’ll lose. And then I’ll be executed.
Despair crept in as he analyzed his options.
There seems to be no way out. No other viable options to survive this.

His Black Hole technique—the devastating attack he believed would be genuinely effective against these powerful opponents—took far too long to properly cast and channel. He’d be caught and killed before completing it; that’s why he never used it before.
Nothing else works! This creature seems to be tracking me like a cat hunting a moth trapped in a sealed room!
Sooner or later, he would be done for. His illusion wasn’t working to hide him. Teleportation only bought seconds.
The roaring, thunderous cheering from the audience continued in the background, a dreadful soundtrack to his impending doom.
"KRESH! KRESH! KRESH!"
And soon, the inevitable moment arrived. The cooldown timer expired, and his temporary boost ended.
His affinity levels dropped from Rank 8 back to Rank 7 across all elements except Ice, which remained at its new permanent Rank 9.
All his abilities and techniques—his elemental raw power, his speed, his defenses—everything became noticeably weaker in an instant.
FIZZLE! CRACK!
No! Not now!
The creature immediately capitalized on his weakened state.
A concentrated ray of blazing fire erupted from the massive beast’s mouth, tracking his movement perfectly.
FWOOOOSH!
This time, it connected directly.
Leon’s entire right arm—from the shoulder joint down—was caught in the beam’s path.
"AHHHHHHH!"

It was completely obliterated, vaporized by the deadly concentrated heat. His epic sword, which somehow didn’t melt despite the intense temperature, fell away from his destroyed hand and dropped toward the arena floor far below.
CLANG! THUD!
The weapon hit the ground intact, resulting in a thunderous, booming cheer from everyone watching. The entire arena physically shook from the collective roar.
"KRESH! KRESH! KRESH!"

But only one person—the girl standing on the stair just below the highest step, Crimson—had a genuinely worried expression on her face. Her fists were clenched tightly and visibly shaking with anxiety and fear.
No... please not him...
Leon teleported again desperately, writhing in absolute agony while suspended in the Air. Intense screams were released continuously from his mouth as the pain overwhelmed his senses.
"AHHHHHH! FUCK!"
His mana worked at maximum capacity, channeling Life elemental energy to regrow his destroyed limb from nothing.
SHIMMER! CRACK! GROW!

Just as his arm had even regenerated halfway—bone forming, then muscle, then skin—the audience erupted with genuinely surprised gasps and even louder cheers. This was something completely unbelievable to witness.
"VEL MANDOR! SIKARA!"
He can regrow limbs?! What kind of monster is this outsider?! That might be thier thought behind their gasps.
However, Leon didn’t have the luxury of even catching his breath or recovering properly.
The massive creature was on him again in milliseconds, giving him no respite. Its giant, razor-sharp claw came crashing down toward him with overwhelming force.
SCREECH! SLASH!
"AHHH!"
The claw plunged deep into his side, his ribs audibly cracking and breaking under the tremendous force of the creature’s powerful muscles.
CRACK! CRUNCH!
Blood poured freely from the massive wound, streaming down his body.
Dying... I’m dying...
But he teleported away in desperation one more time before becoming a complete skewer.
FWOOSH!
However, his fate was clearly sealed. He was completely overpowered by this creature after losing his temporary affinity boost. And now there was only one inevitable outcome left for him.

Healing was consuming a humongous, unsustainable amount of mana. Soon his reserves would be completely depleted, his mana recovery would not be able to catch up with his demands, and then it would finally be over.
This is it. I’m going to die here. In this arena. In front of thousands of cheering spectators who are cheering my demise.
Leon’s thought echoed desperately through his fading consciousness as blood loss and mana depletion took their toll.
"WHHHYYYYYYY!!!! WHY IS THIS ALWAYS HAPPENING TO MEEEEE?!"
His anguished scream was drowned out by another deafening cheer as the creature closed in for the final strike.

chapters.title: Chapter 359: Mark of Fate
paragraphs: The next attack came far too fast for Leon to properly react. The creature’s massive claw slashed across his chest mid-flight.
SLASH!
Blood sprayed through the air in a crimson arc.
"AHHH!"
Leon teleported desperately in the middle of being torn apart, his body covered in deep cuts and gashes. The previous wounds had barely started healing when new ones opened across his torso and legs.
FWOOSH!

Blood poured continuously from multiple wounds. His mana was being sucked away like water through a sponge, converting into brilliant green Life energy that desperately tried to knit his flesh back together.
SHIMMER! CRACK! HEAL!
The brutal cycle continued for what felt like an eternity. Attack. Teleport. Bleed. Heal. Attack again.
Each time, Leon grew weaker. Each time, the healing took longer.
Until finally, inevitably, his mana reserves were completely finished—drained to nothing.
Empty. I’m completely empty.
And now the terrifying creature violently caught his broken body between its enormous claws, the sharp talons piercing through his sides.
CRUNCH! SQUEEZE!
The claws were slick and bloody, covered entirely in his own blood.
"Urgh..."
The massive beast began descending toward the ground, carrying its captured prey down to its master—the woman standing calmly on the arena floor below.
Leon’s mana was slowly recovering through his natural regeneration, drop by precious drop. He could potentially try to teleport away one more time since the technique didn’t require too much energy.
I could escape the grip for a few seconds.
However, he saw absolutely no point in doing so when he was this hurt, this weak, this utterly defeated.
The creature would just catch me again immediately. And experiencing how painful and violent its claws are with the force of those giant muscles... I can’t. I just can’t do it again.
Leon didn’t want to experience that agony another time.
Knowing that teleporting again would be completely futile with the little mana he’d barely gathered, he simply didn’t attempt it.
What’s the point? I’ve lost.

In the background, he could hear the thunderous cheers from the massive crowd as his broken body was unceremoniously dropped onto the hard ground by the creature, landing directly in front of the girl with her fiery armor and blazing greatsword strapped to her back.
THUD!
"KRESH! KRESH! KRESH! VEL MANDOR!"
The noises were like rolling thunder in his ears, making his head pound. Everything felt utterly pointless as he lay there weak and defeated.
I couldn’t even win against her pet. Winning against her directly was always just a pathetic dream.
A terrible realization crashed over him like ice water.
Does that mean I have to die now? After I admit defeat, that psychotic man will execute me?
But why?
Why does it always have to be me?
Why, why, why?
The crowd’s roar became a painful ringing in his head. The woman in the fiery armor stood directly over him, looking down with her blazing crimson eyes.
The scent of scorched flesh filled his nostrils, and the hot stone beneath his back pulsed with radiant heat, as if mocking his weakness.
She said something in her harsh language, her massive sword positioned right next to his exposed chest.
His invisible armor was completely destroyed. His barely-healed skin was already sizzling painfully from the intense heat radiating from her technique.
SIZZLE... CRACK...
But Leon was mentally checked out—completely dissociated, trapped deep inside his own tortured mind. The physical pain couldn’t reach him anymore, couldn’t gain his attention now.
Since the moment I came to this cursed world, I’ve been constantly getting into life-threatening situations. My existence has always been on the edge of death, somehow.
His thoughts spiraled backward through his suffering.
First, I nearly died inside the Awakening Dungeon on my very first day.

Then it seemed like that was my only major test. But no—due to my Holy energy incompatibility, I was tortured for an entire subjective year to forcibly build my mana heart. I barely survived by dying repeatedly and being revived over and over by the Phoenix Tears treasure I’d bought.
Then I finally got my new Divinordial race, which promised unimaginable power and strength beyond mortal limits.

I genuinely thought I didn’t have to be weak anymore after that transformation. But then again, in Thornwood Forest, I encountered the Coreborn monster Morpheus, which nearly took my life anyway, despite my new power. I only survived by desperately exploiting my time dimension.
I thought I’d finally escaped that fate of constantly nearly dying. The supreme leaders of the middle domain had to bow down to me and accept my demands! I felt powerful! Safe!
But no. Here I am now, trapped in this unknown, hostile world, just lying helpless on the ground waiting to die. And if I lose and surrender, that monstrous man will execute me without hesitation.
Despair consumed him entirely.
I’m not strong enough to even escape this time. No tricks left. No trump cards. Nothing.
Do I really have to die now? Here? Like this?
Nooo... I don’t want that. This second life was so, so much better than my previous existence. I finally had someone who truly loves me.
Seraphine’s face appeared in his mind, smiling at him.
Everything was finally good. But why? Why, why, WHY am I getting thrown into these damn death situations over and over and over and OVER again?!
That faint feeling—the one he’d been ignoring for so long—was still there, lurking at the edge of his awareness.
That wrongness. That sense of being... manipulated.
Leon suddenly shouted with everything he had left, his voice carrying past the deafening cheering of the arena, past the woman looking down on him, waiting for his surrender.
"WHOOO ARE YOUUUUU?!"
His desperate scream echoed.
"AND WHY ARE YOU AFTER MY LIFE?!"
In a world that crossed the barrier between universes.
Inside a mighty, grand throne room stretching impossibly far and wide—yet filled with only emptiness and ancient, suffocating silence.
A single being sat motionless upon an ornate throne, eyes that had been closed for... who knows how long.
Centuries.
Millennia.
Perhaps even longer.
No one but the being itself knew the true answer to that question.
But those ancient eyes had opened some time ago—watching the boy lying bloodied on the distant arena floor, listening to his desperate shout carried across dimensional barriers.
The being smiled slightly, an expression both amused and contemplative.
Its voice, ancient and resonant with power beyond comprehension, spoke words in a dialect lost to time:

"So... this unnatural existence cannot yet bear the weight of the Primordial Mark of Fate. Will this be his end? Even I cannot tell what lies ahead. Even incomplete as he is, I cannot peer into his future. That is the nature of us Divinordial—no force in existence can measure or predict our destinies with certainty."
Leon received no answer to his desperate question.
But a shimmering golden screen slowly revealed itself before his blurred vision, the text glowing with otherworldly light.
The air itself shivered faintly, brushing his skin with static warmth—as if the system’s presence rippled through the world like a god inhaling.
[CONGRATULATIONS]
[You have consciously noticed the influence of your PRIMORDIAL MARK OF FATE]
[May Fate favor you in the trials ahead]
Leon’s eyes went impossibly wide as he read everything displayed.
What... what is this?!

He knew with absolute certainty he wasn’t imagining this. Since the time he’d awakened his SSS Rank Elemental Paragon Class, there had been something—really, really faint back then, almost imperceptible.
But after his race change to Divinordial, it had become slightly less faint. Still subtle, but... present. Always present.
That feeling. That wrongness. It was THIS. This whole time!

No one but the being itself knew the true answer to that question.
But those ancient eyes had opened some time ago—watching the boy lying bloodied on the distant arena floor, listening to his desperate shout carried across dimensional barriers.
The being smiled slightly, an expression both amused and contemplative.
Its voice, ancient and resonant with power beyond comprehension, spoke words in a dialect lost to time:
"So... this unnatural existence cannot yet bear the weight of the Primordial Mark of Fate.
Will this be his end?
Even I cannot tell what lies ahead.
Even incomplete as he is, I cannot peer into his future.
That is the nature of us Divinordial—no force in existence can measure or predict our destinies with certainty."
Leon received no answer to his desperate question.
But a shimmering golden screen slowly revealed itself before his blurred vision, the text glowing with otherworldly light.
The air itself shivered faintly, brushing his skin with static warmth—as if the system’s presence rippled through the world like a god inhaling.
[CONGRATULATIONS]
[You have consciously noticed the influence of your PRIMORDIAL MARK OF FATE]
[May Fate favor you in the trials ahead]
Leon’s eyes went impossibly wide as he read everything displayed.
What... what is this?!
He knew with absolute certainty he wasn’t imagining this.
Since the time he’d awakened his SSS Rank Elemental Paragon Class, there had been something—really, really faint back then, almost imperceptible.
But after his race change to Divinordial, it had become slightly less faint.
Still subtle, but... present.
Always present.
That feeling.
That wrongness.
It was THIS.
This whole time!

chapters.title: Chapter 360: Fighting Fate
paragraphs: That feeling. That wrongness. It was THIS. This whole time!
Understanding crashed over him, and with it came pure, incandescent rage.
"I don’t want any of this!" he screamed with everything he had. "I don’t want whatever this ’Mark of Fate’ is that’s influencing my life!"
I’m not some toy in someone’s grand game! I’m not a puppet!
He shouted again at the top of his lungs, ignoring everything happening around him. The crowd, the woman, the arena—all of it blurred into meaningless background noise.
"I DON’T WANT ANY OF THIS!!! TAKE IT BACK!!!"
He desperately didn’t want his life influenced and manipulated by some unknown cosmic power that was systematically making his new life hell.
I just want to live peacefully on my own terms! With Seraphine! Building my harem! Living freely! Is that too much to ask?!
However, everything remained silent—no answer came from whatever entity or force he was trying to reach.
While Leon could subconsciously block out and ignore the physical world around him in his mental state, that didn’t mean it wouldn’t affect him.
The woman’s massive flaming sword came crashing down—not the edge, but the flat side—slamming brutally into his ribs.
CRASH! SIZZLE!
"AHHH!"
The searing heat and blunt force sent him rolling across the arena floor with a painful grunt, shocking him violently back to his senses and the real world.
The metal’s scorching touch seared through bone and nerve, leaving the scent of burning skin in its wake.

Back to the desperate situation he was actually in. Back to the deafening cheers filling the arena. Back to Crimson, who was now on ground level just outside the combat circle, visibly holding herself back from interfering with the match. Her teeth were gritted, and she was shouting something desperately to him in her language—words he couldn’t hear clearly and wouldn’t understand anyway.
"VEL KRESH! TOR MANDOR! VEL!"
Leon felt the burning, agonizing pain radiating from his side where the superheated sword had struck.
Pain. Always more pain.
He was thoroughly accustomed to pain by now—how could he not be after being tortured so many times? However, that familiarity didn’t mean he liked it or accepted it.
I hate this. I hate all of it.
The Mark of Fate is manipulating his life. The woman is hurting him right now. The monstrous man who would kill him after he accepted defeat.
I hate every single one of them.
What had he done to deserve any of this torment?
His eyes turned bloodshot red. His teeth ground together audibly as he looked up at the woman standing over him, her fiery sword raised above his broken body once more.
I’m so angry. So incredibly angry.
She said something loudly in her harsh language, probably demanding his surrender.
"VEL KRESH MANDOR TOR!"
Leon had absolutely had enough. One-fourth of his mana had slowly recovered through his passive regeneration.
Enough. I’m done with this.
Without replying or acknowledging her at all, Leon attempted to teleport away—
But she disrupted the technique instantly with that red energy field surrounding her, locking down his spatial manipulation.
FIZZLE! BZZZZT!
No! Damn it!
Her eyes seemed to make a final decision then. Her expression hardened with determination.
He won’t surrender. So I’ll force him to stop fighting, or worse, If It continued like this...
Her blazing sword struck directly downward, aimed at both his legs with clear intent to sever them completely.
If he can’t stand or move, the match ends. Simple.
Leon’s eyes tracked her descending sword with horrified clarity.
The pain is going to hit me again. I don’t want that. Please, no more.
"Nooo..."
Stop it. Please stop.
His anger was reaching an absolute peak, boiling over into something primal.
I don’t want any of this! Why? Why me?!
His mind was losing control, rational thought fragmenting.
From the very depths of his tortured soul, he screamed at the top of his lungs with every ounce of will he possessed:
"STOPPPPPPPP!!!"
An unknown power exploded outward from Leon’s body, spreading across the entire massive arena in an invisible wave.
A cold pressure expanded like a heartbeat through space, distorting the air like a lens and brushing every skin it touched with weightless force.
WHUMMMMM!
The woman in fiery armor with her giant descending sword suddenly paused mid-strike—frozen completely.
Not just her.
The flying beast circling overhead locked in place, wings spread but motionless.
It didn’t stop there.
The unknown power affected almost everyone inside and around the arena. Those watching from the giant steps—thousands of spectators—were caught in the effect.

Everyone below the Ascendant rank was frozen completely still in their place, locked like statues. Those at the Ascendant rank felt the power wash over them strongly for several seconds, struggling against it. Above Ascendant—those at Sage rank and higher—they merely felt its presence subtly but continued moving just fine, largely unaffected.
What... what is this power?!
In that same moment, along with his desperate scream, Leon felt something tear violently inside his throat.
CRACK! RIP!
Blood erupted from his mouth as internal damage manifested. He was coughing up blood continuously, experiencing intense pain throughout his neck and chest.
COUGH! COUGH! SPLATTER!
My throat... it’s destroyed...
He could feel the blood pooling inside, taste copper and iron.
But those overwhelming, intense emotions—that absolute desperation and rage—had not only let his Lexiomancy racial ability break loose uncontrollably for the first time...
It had also awakened something else that had been carefully tamed and controlled for far too long.
His Holy energy is dormant and suppressed deep in his core.
Only a slip was enough. Just one moment of lost control.
The Holy energy burst forth like a devastating tsunami, an unstoppable flood.
WHOOOOOOSH! SHIMMER!
It devoured all his remaining mana in milliseconds, converting everything into pure golden-white radiance.
The entire arena fell into stunned, absolute silence.
It was like the world had been turned mute—no breeze, no cheers, no rumble of excitement, not even the subtle hum of voices. Just absolute, crushing stillness.
Most spectators were frozen, even their eyes locked in place—but those eyes were all focused on the arena center as they had been before the freeze took effect.
Where now there was only a silhouetted figure consumed entirely by brilliant golden-white light, radiant and overwhelming.
SHIMMER! GLOW! RADIATE!
All of Leon’s wounds healed in an instant—flesh knitting, bones mending, blood replenishing.
CRACK! HEAL! SHIMMER!
Leon stood up—no, he was floating now, hovering above the ground without using the elemental combination flight technique he’d relied on before.
I’m... flying? Just from this energy alone?
He looked directly in front of him. The woman was frozen in place, her fiery sword suspended mid-swing exactly where it had been about to strike and cripple him.
To make me feel more pain. Pain I didn’t want or deserve.
The Vice Chief, standing on the highest step, was watching all of this unfold with an expression of absolute peak curiosity and fascination—nothing more, no fear or concern.
Interesting. Very interesting indeed.
Leon, consumed by rage and Holy energy, punched the frozen woman’s body directly in her chest over her protective armor.
BOOM!
A loud impact sound echoed across the silent arena.
But... nothing happened. Her armor was strong enough to completely block his strength without even cracking.
"WHYYY?! You can hurt me whenever you want, and I can’t even SCRATCH you?!"
He was even more enraged than before, the injustice of it all crushing him.
It’s not fair! Nothing is fair!
He punched again and again, over and over. He was absolutely enraged, though even through his fury, he knew logically she wouldn’t remain frozen for much longer.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
He punched hundreds of times in just seconds, his fists moving in desperate blurs.

chapters.title: Chapter 361: Fighting Fate—2
paragraphs: Leon punched again and again, over and over. He was absolutely enraged, though even through his fury, he knew logically she wouldn’t remain frozen for much longer.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
He punched hundreds of times in just seconds, his fists moving in desperate blurs.
But he wasn’t even able to get past her enchanted armor’s defensive properties.
Every punch came with a desperate denial: "NOOO!"
And a tormented question: "WHHYYY?!"
And deep inside, beneath the rage and Holy energy, he knew the real answer.
Because I can’t even use my full power. I can only access roughly fifteen percent of my actual physical strength.
"AHHHHHHH!"
He absolutely couldn’t accept this limitation anymore.
I refuse! I REFUSE!
He tried desperately to push past the limit, to break through the barrier.
And unexpectedly—unbelievably—something happened, on his very first try.
As if a gateway to an entirely new world had been opened with just a slight push forward...
It happened.
CRACK! WHOOOOSH!
He crossed the unknown limit that had bound him.
Unimaginable strength flooded his body all at once, far beyond anything he’d felt before.

An overwhelming pressure filled the entire arena—the ground directly below where he hovered, which hadn’t suffered even a scratch since the arena’s ancient construction, suddenly cracked deeply just from the ambient force.
CRACK! CRUMBLE!
"This is it! I can use it! I can access my real strength!"
Leon then detected—without even needing his spatial awareness—that she was breaking free. Her sword was moving again, coming toward him much faster and stronger than before.
Her eyes looked completely different now—fully aware, calculating, and dangerous.
She’s free!
Leon hovered smoothly to the side, out of the path of her descending sword with casual ease.
WHOOSH!
But to the audience members who were breaking free from the freeze effect now, too, they remained absolutely dead silent. Their eyes were glued to the brilliant, glowing figure, unable to look away.
Their breath held collectively. Many of them were visibly shaking—from excitement, fear, awe, or some combination. Who could tell?
What is that light? What is that being?
Leon dodged her sword and immediately punched the exact same place—her chest, her fiery, intense armor’s strongest point.
His glowing fist connected with her protective layer.
IMPACT!
For a single frozen moment, it seemed as if nothing would happen—just like all the times before.
Then visible cracks began spreading across her previously impenetrable armor like a spiderweb.
CRACK! CRACK! CRACK!
The woman’s eyes went impossibly wide with shock and disbelief.
Impossible! My armor—!
Then Leon’s strike connected fully with her actual body beneath the failing protection.
BOOOOOOOOOOMMMMM!

A massive sonic explosion erupted from the point of impact, sending devastating shockwaves rippling through the entire arena—traveling through the stone, through the air, through every person’s skin, and rattling their bones.
The stone beneath the crowd vibrated, and many in the front rows clutched their chests, feeling the pulse echo through their ribcages.
BOOM! RUMBLE! SHAKE!
The Vice Chief’s expression shifted instantly from curiosity to extreme seriousness, his eyes narrowing with focus and intensity.
That power... what IS he?!

Crimson, standing on the ground floor just outside the arena boundary, looked absolutely shocked beyond words. Then suddenly she was smiling—widely, genuinely—her body shaking visibly with overwhelming emotion.
She was caught between excitement and fear, completely overwhelmed by surprise and a dozen other feelings she couldn’t name.
"VEL KRESH! MANDOR! SIKARA!"
He’s... he’s actually... so strong...
The woman felt intense, searing pain exploding across her entire chest cavity—agony unlike anything she’d experienced in years of brutal combat.
What... what just happened?!

She could feel distinctly that several of her actual ribs were broken—fractured cleanly through by that devastating punch. This injury would take considerable time to heal properly, even for someone of her Sage rank cultivation.
I can’t accept this! This is impossible!
She’d genuinely felt he was weak and pathetic, so she’d been deliberately holding back, going easy on him. But now? This felt extreme and terrifying.
My armor... my technique-forged protection... broken in one single punch. How is this even remotely possible?!
Her mind raced with shock and calculation.
I have to go all out. Immediately. No more testing. No more mercy.
As she was flying backward through the air from the force of his devastating strike, she burst her Fire affinity outward in all opposite directions simultaneously to create momentum and control.
FWOOOOSH! WHOOSH!
Using the explosive counter-thrust, she arrested her backward flight and stabilized herself mid-air.

Then she immediately recreated her protective armor using her racial ability’s special Fire manifestation technique—but this time, she tapped fully into her Fire Embodiment, not just barely touching it like she’d done before in the fight.
CRACKLE! WHOOOOSH! SHIMMER!
The advanced fire energy merged seamlessly with her reformed armor, creating something far more substantial. Her greatsword became covered in that same overwhelming intensity.
This is my true power. My real form.

The armor was dramatically more advanced than her previous version—this wasn’t just condensed elemental energy anymore. It appeared as an actual physical manifestation of her complete power—solid, tangible, and radiating devastating heat.
SHIMMER! GLOW! RADIATE!
Waves of heat radiated from her body, distorting the air around her in liquid ripples, and the faint scent of scorched iron filled the air.
She looked like a miniature red destroyer—a war goddess.
Fully armored from head to toe with her giant flaming sword, she floated above the ground on a platform of pure fire beneath her feet.
CRACKLE! WHOOSH!
Her chest wounds were still hurting intensely from the broken ribs, sending sharp pain with every breath. But she deliberately ignored the agony and pushed through.
Pain doesn’t matter. Winning matters.
She was ready to charge directly at him with everything she possessed.
However, when she looked forward toward where he’d been standing...
There was no one in front of her.
What? Where—?
"Huh?"
Then she heard a voice directly next to her left side—far too close.
"It’s time for payback."
FWOOSH!
Leon’s glowing fist struck her newly formed armor once again before she could even begin to react or defend. She was simply too slow compared to his Holy-energy-enhanced speed.
Too fast! How is he—?!
The entire arena collectively held its breath, thousands of eyes locked on the point of impact.
IMPACT!
The connection was made with devastating force—this time targeting her abdomen specifically.
CRACK! BOOM!
The noise was sharp and grinding, like boulders splitting under unbearable weight.
Visible cracks spread across her advanced armor plating despite its improved construction.
But this time, Leon caught the horrified expression on her face clearly—her eyes going wide with genuine fear and disbelief.
A single word escaped her mouth loudly in her native language, audible even over the impact:
"KRESH’THOR!"
Then—
BOOOOOOOM!

Another massive sonic shockwave rippled across the entire arena, which had fallen into absolute deadly silence. Everyone was witnessing the same impossible result playing out again, and they still couldn’t believe how the situation had reversed so dramatically in just mere moments, and now one of the strongest warrior of their clan was getting beaten so brutally.
"VEL... MANDOR..."
She went flying backward violently, her lower ribcage completely shattered now. Multiple organs were damaged internally from the transmitted force.
An acidic burn spread through her gut as ruptured tissue screamed from within, every breath laced with agony.
CRASH!
This time, she absolutely couldn’t hold it in anymore—blood gushed freely from her mouth in a violent spray, painting the air red.
SPLATTER! COUGH!
I’m... I’m losing?! To the same weak him?! Impossible!
Just then, Leon detected something approaching rapidly from directly behind his back through his senses alone.
I was waiting for you make a move! It’s about time.

Then she heard a voice directly next to her left side—far too close.
"It’s time for payback."
FWOOSH!
Leon’s glowing fist struck her newly formed armor once again before she could even begin to react or defend.
She was simply too slow compared to his Holy-energy-enhanced speed.
Too fast!
How is he—?!
The entire arena collectively held its breath, thousands of eyes locked on the point of impact.
IMPACT!
The connection was made with devastating force—this time targeting her abdomen specifically.
CRACK!
BOOM!
The noise was sharp and grinding, like boulders splitting under unbearable weight.
Visible cracks spread across her advanced armor plating despite its improved construction.
But this time, Leon caught the horrified expression on her face clearly—her eyes going wide with genuine fear and disbelief.
A single word escaped her mouth loudly in her native language, audible even over the impact:
"KRESH’THOR!"
Then—
BOOOOOOOM!
Another massive sonic shockwave rippled across the entire arena, which had fallen into absolute deadly silence.

Everyone was witnessing the same impossible result playing out again, and they still couldn’t believe how the situation had reversed so dramatically in just mere moments, and now one of the strongest warrior of their clan was getting beaten so brutally.
"VEL...
MANDOR..."
She went flying backward violently, her lower ribcage completely shattered now.
Multiple organs were damaged internally from the transmitted force.
An acidic burn spread through her gut as ruptured tissue screamed from within, every breath laced with agony.
CRASH!
This time, she absolutely couldn’t hold it in anymore—blood gushed freely from her mouth in a violent spray, painting the air red.
SPLATTER!
COUGH!
I’m losing?!
To the same weak him?!
Impossible!
Just then, Leon detected something approaching rapidly from directly behind his back through his senses alone.
I was waiting for you make a move!
It’s about time.

chapters.title: Chapter 362: Fighting Fate—3
paragraphs: Behind Leon was the same massive red flying companion of the woman—the creature that had made him suffer so much excruciating pain and rendered him completely helpless before.
Perfect timing. I was just about to come for you anyway.
Leon was genuinely pleased it had attacked on its own initiative—this gave him the perfect opportunity to repay every debt of suffering it had inflicted.
Let’s settle this.
He turned like a blinking light—impossibly fast. The creature’s giant claw was descending toward him with tremendous force, though notably it was blazing with fire this time.
Trying to crush me physically? Mistake.

But Leon wasn’t even fazed or concerned. Until this very moment, he hadn’t been using any of the actual abilities the Holy element itself inherently provided—he’d only been utilizing the unlocked physical strength it granted access to.
Time to show what Holy energy can really do.
Leon concentrated his Holy energy specifically around his right fist, compressing it into a dense, radiant layer. Then he punched directly toward the incoming claw with his full unlocked force.
WHOOSH! IMPACT!
He still hadn’t boosted his base strength further with additional Holy energy enhancement because he genuinely didn’t think he had any need to against this creature.
This should be more than enough.
The clash happened with devastating results.
BOOM! CRACK!
The residual fire that had been concentrated on the creature’s claw was instantly dispersed and extinguished by the sheer force of Leon’s strike.
But the destruction didn’t stop there.
CRACK! SNAP!
The impact jolted up creature paw like it was thunder.
One of the creature’s three massive claws broke cleanly in half, the bone and cartilage shattering audibly.
This resulted in a gut-wrenching, agonized screech from the beast, released at maximum volume from its beak-like mouth, along with a thunderous shockwave rippling outward.
SCREEEEECH! BOOM!
The creature writhed violently in pain, thrashing in the air.
Meanwhile, Leon remained completely unharmed—he hadn’t taken any damage whatsoever from the exchange.
My body feels so much stronger when using Holy energy fully, compared to when I rely on mana. It’s not even close.
As the creature continued writhing and screeching in agony, Leon didn’t stop his assault. He grabbed hold of one of its other intact claws with both hands.
GRIP!
Then he planted his right leg firmly on the ground with tremendous force—
CRASH! CRACK!
—which made the solid arena floor cave in deeply beneath the impact point, creating a crater.

Using that anchored position as leverage, Leon violently flipped the massive creature’s entire body over and then slammed it brutally onto the hard, red floor of the arena, which was supposedly constructed from extremely solid material.
CRASH! BOOM!
He slammed it again and again like it was nothing more than a bag filled with cotton, treating the enormous beast like a ragdoll.
SLAM! CRASH! SLAM! CRASH!
The repeated impacts continued until the claw Leon was gripping finally went completely limp.
The creature’s body was now thoroughly bloody and broken. It was still writhing weakly in pain, twitching pathetically.
Not done yet? Good. I’m not satisfied either.

But the beast wasn’t fully defeated yet when he left it withering on the ground. Leon observed as its massive mouth opened wide, its eyes barely able to focus through the blood and pain, barely standing on its feet. Despite its condition, it was still attempting to fire that same devastatingly powerful concentrated fire beam from before.
Stubborn thing.

He smiled, appreciating its defiance. That just gave him more reason to make itsuffer.Because I’m still not feeling content about how it tortured me before, when I was desperately trying to escape from its grasp.
Leon deliberately let the creature accumulate power for its attack. He could see it was gathering energy for what appeared to be the most powerful fire beam it had produced yet.
He smiled almost devilishly because he already had a clear plan in mind for what he was going to do the moment it fired.
With my current speed, this will be easy.
He could already visualize the creature’s head exploding into pieces in his mind, playing out the sequence.
Three seconds until it fires. Two seconds. One—
Then he detected her approaching rapidly from behind—the woman warrior, moving fast by normal standards, slower than before, still appearing slow to his enhanced perception.
She’s coming. Still trying to fight despite her injuries. Brave, but foolish.
Leon waited patiently, keeping most of his focus on the creature in front, which was still generating more and more power for its ultimate attack.
The air reeked of sulfur and scorched ozone, heatwaves distorting the space between them.
He could feel the heat building, the energy condensing.

The audience remained absolutely silent even now, stunned into speechlessness. Watching this unknown outsider brutally beating one of their strongest warriors and her powerful beast companion was initially entertaining when it was an equal fight.
But now? The power difference seemed impossibly wide, appearing out of nowhere.
They’re scared now. Good.

Leon continued waiting for the creature, knowing with absolute certainty it would die with this next move. And he felt absolutely nothing—no guilt, no hesitation—because he himself would have died to this creature’s violent attacks in the air if not for his life elemental ability.
It tried to kill me. Now I return the favor.
The concentrated beam finally erupted from the creature’s mouth, making Leon’s smile widen inside the brilliant golden-white light surrounding him.
FWOOOOSH!
The woman still hadn’t reached his position yet—she seemed so slow compared to before in his enhanced senses. She was clearly severely hurt, struggling with each movement.
Too slow. Too late.

Leon moved in a blinking instant, positioning himself directly below the creature’s head so fast that its beam had only just left its mouth. He was already in a position to finish it using his own attack’s momentum.
His fist drew back, ready to punch through its skull—
But suddenly, a loud voice thundered across the arena in a single commanding word.
"KRESH’THOR!"
Leon ignored it completely and continued his strike.
Just as he was about to connect with devastating force, he suddenly detected something extremely fast approaching him from the side.
I was waiting for you!

chapters.title: Chapter 363: Fighting Fate—4
paragraphs: Leon could sense it clearly now—arriving right next to his position with incredible speed, forcing him to shift his focus from the creature.
This was no simple defensive maneuver.
Him. Of course it’s him.
Leon immediately redirected his punch toward the new threat, recognizing the presence instantly through his enhanced senses.

And this time, he didn’t hold back his Holy energy enhancement at all. He boosted his base physical strength by over ten percent more, channeling Holy energy directly for the first time, beyond just unlocking his sealed physique.
Let’s see you block this.
There he was—the same terrifying man from before, the Vice Chief who’d threatened Leon’s life repeatedly.
In front of Leon’s incoming fist was a swirling red defensive shield constructed from hundreds of small hexagonal shapes, all interlocking and reinforcing each other.
So you decided to interfere personally. I was expecting this.

Leon had genuinely expected this bastard who wanted him dead to interfere somehow, and when he’d noticed the man descending to the ground floor at the arena’s edge half a minute earlier, he’d been even more certain.
Here we go.
His Holy-energy-enhanced punch connected directly with the hexagonal shield.
BOOOOOOOOMMMMM!
The biggest shockwave that had ever occurred in the arena’s history erupted from the impact point.
RUMBLE! SHAKE! CRACK!

The dying creature next to them—whose misdirected fire beam was now heading dangerously toward the crowd—went flying like a broken ragdoll from just the ambient shockwave alone, its bloody body tumbling through the air.
SCREECH! CRASH!

Along with the woman who’d been fighting Leon before, still on her knees some distance away with blood pouring from her mouth and multiple broken bones—she was also caught in the devastating shockwave and thrown backward.
CRASH!
Their eyes met and locked as Leon’s fist connected with the shield, and visible cracks began forming across its surface.
The man’s eyes widened noticeably—though only slightly—at seeing his defensive technique actually damaged.
He’s surprised. Good.
However, the cracks quickly started being repaired as massive amounts of red energy began flowing from the man into the shield, reinforcing its structure.
Regenerating defense. Interesting.
But Leon was far from finished.
Who was this bastard to decide whether I live or die? I can escape to my time dimension anytime now if needed.
He wasn’t worried anymore. And more importantly, this display was nowhere near his full strength in this Holy energy form—he was barely utilizing the complete power available to him.
Let’s increase the pressure.
Leon gave himself a twenty percent strength boost this time, channeling significantly more Holy energy into raw physical enhancement.
His holy aura rippled outward like a sonic tide, the very air crackling with sanctified pressure that made dust rise from the arena floor.
Then he punched again with devastating force.
His knuckles throbbed from the collision, Holy energy still sizzling across his skin like divine lightning.
BOOOOOOOM!
The shockwave alone from this second strike was hurting many weaker spectators in the arena, causing them to clutch their ears and chests in pain.
Inside the combat zone, the woman and the dying creature were being thrown around like leaves in a storm.
This time, the hexagonal shield broke completely and shattered under Leon’s punch.
CRACK! SHATTER!
His fist connected directly with the man’s red crossed arms, which he’d raised at the last instant to block after his shield failed.
The impact resulted in the Vice Chief being pushed backward several steps, with visible burn marks appearing on his forearms where Leon’s Holy energy had made contact.
SKID! SKID! SKID!
The man’s eyes widened fully this time, genuinely shocked at feeling the true strength behind that attack.
My shield... completely destroyed. And his power increased so suddenly to such an extreme degree. What is this energy?
The Vice Chief said something loudly to Leon in his language, his tone carrying what sounded like a challenge or warning.
"Vel’kresh mandor sikara TOR KALA VEL!"
But to Leon, it just seemed like the man was issuing a challenge. Since he’d already interfered with the match and was clearly willing to fight, Leon had made his decision.
I’m going to try to kill you if possible. You decided my fate before—now I’ll decide yours.

The girl—he still wasn’t certain what he would have done with her ultimately, since she’d had multiple chances to kill him but deliberately hadn’t, using the flat of her blade. It seemed she didn’t want lethal involvement.
Maybe she deserves mercy.
But the creature? It had made him feel far too much pain and suffering. He had absolutely no mercy for it whatsoever.
It dies. No question.
The Vice Chief’s words were completely deaf to Leon’s ears. He wasn’t listening or caring.
Meanwhile, Crimson was desperately trying to get closer to them, shouting something frantically. But she wasn’t able to approach because the continuous shockwaves kept forcing her back.
"VEL KRESH! MANDOR!"
Leon checked the man’s status information for the first time, no longer worried about being detected since they were already fighting.
[Level 69 - Sage Rank]
His level is only eight above the woman’s, but his strength is vastly incomparable. Which means he’s extremely close to breaking through to Archon rank.
That explained the massive power gap.
The Vice Chief repeated the same words as before, and Leon could see a solid red armor beginning to materialize around the man’s entire body.
But it didn’t look like traditional armor—it appeared as if it was part of his actual skin, layering over him in countless very small hexagonal segments that covered every inch.
SHIMMER! FORM! SOLIDIFY!
The energy contained within those segments seemed absolutely massive and condensed.
Impressive technique. But I’m not worried.
Leon wanted to genuinely test his full strength if possible. And if the opportunity presented itself, he was absolutely going to kill this motherfucker who had caused him so much torment and fear.
Yes, I discovered my Holy power’s ability to unlock my sealed strength. But that doesn’t justify or forgive what you put me through.
Similar to the Vice Chief’s armor technique, Leon attempted to form a protective layer around himself as well.
It didn’t look nearly as refined as the man’s long practiced technique.
It was crude, yes. But pulsing with unfiltered power. Divine energy forged not by technique, but raw will.
He already have a defensive skill similar to this concept in my Ice affinity, which helped him succeed on the first attempt. Though it needs refinement.
And not only that defensive measure—he also boosted his base strength directly with Holy energy enhancement to fifty percent above his sealed baseline.
WHOOOOSH! SHIMMER! GLOW!
The entire arena felt the massive jump in his power level, along with the Vice Chief, whose expression shifted dramatically and was definitely not looking confident anymore.
Even the highest step of arena above vibrated faintly, and a faint ringing echoed in the ears of the every spectators—like being too close to a bell tower mid-strike.

chapters.title: Chapter 364: New Arrival
paragraphs: The entire arena felt the massive jump in his power level, along with the Vice Chief, whose expression shifted dramatically and was definitely not looking confident anymore.
He feels it. He knows this is serious now.
In the man’s hand materialized a full-length red sword with intricate golden markings running along its blade—clearly a weapon of exceptional quality.
Leon decided to try something on instinct. He stretched out his right hand and thought strongly about his weapon.
Come to me.
WHOOSH!
It worked immediately. Leon felt his sword’s emotion—its eagerness, its loyalty—and he called, and it came flying to him across the arena.
Into his palm arrived his epic-ranked sword, which had previously appeared as a high-quality black blade. But now, the moment it came into contact with his tremendous Holy energy...
SHIMMER! TREMBLE! GLOW!
The sword started vibrating intensely, then began absorbing his Holy energy like an endless, bottomless well—drinking in the power greedily.
Take what you need. I have plenty.

Leon didn’t stop the flow. He had accumulated far too much Holy energy inside himself over the months and years it had been building, generated continuously by his unknown believers across dimensions.
The sword’s appearance transformed completely, taking on a brilliant, glowing golden-white color that pulsed with divine radiance.
Leon’s palm tingled, almost burning, as the sword drank deeper, pulsing in sync with his heart.
GLOW! SHIMMER! RADIATE!
Leon felt its enhanced power in his hand—it felt like an entirely different weapon from before, elevated to a new tier of existence.
This is incredible. The synergy is perfect.
He wasn’t alone in recognizing the danger. The Vice Chief was also staring at Leon’s transformed sword with visible caution and concern, clearly realizing the genuine threat it represented.
He knows. Smart man.

Leon’s mystical eyes—in which a golden circle had appeared around each iris, spinning rapidly like mechanical gears—locked onto the man with an eager smile, ready to test his newfound power by trying to kill this bastard.
Let’s see what you’re really made of.
However, before both their swords could clash and cause absolute devastation to everything around them in the arena—
A massive shadow suddenly covered the entire arena, blocking out the red sun above.
WHOOOOSH!
A sudden drop in temperature swept the arena as the red sun disappeared, replaced by the eerie shade of the new arrival’s presence.
A visible sigh of relief escaped from the Vice Chief’s mouth.
"Vel’kresh..."
And then, moving like a streak of pure red light—causing no collateral damage or devastation despite the incredible speed—someone appeared between them.
FWOOSH!
She was hovering slightly above the red arena floor.
Her two hands, transformed into red diamond-like crystalline claws of enormous power, caught both weapons simultaneously—Leon’s glowing Holy sword and the Vice Chief’s red blade with golden marking.
A metallic screech sang between her palms as both blades strained against her unmoving claws, the air itself warping from the pressure.
CATCH! GRIP!

A shockwave was created from the interception, but a protective shield materialized instantly around all three of them, completely encasing them in a translucent red barrier and preventing any damage from spreading to the audience or arena.
SHIMMER! SEAL!
What?! Who—?!
It was a new, unexpected arrival.
But Leon was not scared or intimidated by her overwhelming presence, despite feeling the absolutely massive pressure radiating from her body like a physical weight.
Another powerful enemy? Fine. I’ll face them all.
He increased the rate of his Holy energy enhancement dramatically, reaching one hundred percent augmentation of his sealed baseline strength.
WHOOOOSH! CRACKLE! GLOW!
His aura blazed even more brilliantly than before, the golden-white radiance intensifying to near-blinding levels.
SIZZLE! CRACK!
A distinct sizzling sound came from her crystalline red armored hand where it gripped his Holy-infused sword, the divine energy clearly affecting even her defensive technique.
She feels it. Good.
The woman—with glowing hair like liquid fire and golden-marked eyes set in her regal crimson form—hovered slightly above the ground.
She felt his increased power surging against her grip.
Strong human
The Vice Chief standing nearby was genuinely shocked now, his eyes going wide at witnessing the human brazenness and strength against thier leaders, seeing the smoke from her crystalline hand.
Impossible! No one resists HER presence!

Leon’s mystical eyes—with bright golden halos swirling continuously on the edge of each pupil like miniature suns—remained locked and ready to clash despite this new, overwhelmingly powerful being positioned directly between them.
I don’t care who you are. I’m not backing down.
However, then suddenly Leon heard something completely unexpected from the new woman’s mouth.
"Calm down, human. We are not your enemy. This is a misunderstanding—put down your weapon. You will destroy our last remaining city, and I will not allow that to happen at any cost."
SHIMMER!
A circular, bright red halo of pure power appeared behind her head for just a moment—
WHOOOOSH! PRESSURE!

—which instantly forced the Vice Chief to collapse to his knees along with every other person in the entire arena and even beyond its walls. Thousands dropped simultaneously under the weight of her revealed authority.
THUD! CRASH! THUD!
But the human—Leon—was not on his knees.
What? How is he...?
Leon felt the tremendous, overwhelming power contained within her when that halo manifested behind her for that brief second. It was like standing before a god made manifest.
She’s... she’s on a completely different level from everyone here.
The woman’s expression remained calm as she continued speaking.
"So let us talk reasonably."
Her words were not in the harsh Pyrrhan language Leon couldn’t understand—they were spoken in his own native tongue, which made him mentally stumble for a second in pure shock.
She’s speaking... my language? How?!
The fact that he wasn’t forced to his knees like everyone else wasn’t even something he’d consciously tried to resist—it simply was that way naturally, without any effort on his part.
My Holy energy protected me automatically? Or is it my Divinordial nature?
He doesn’t know?
But to this powerful woman, Leon’s natural resistance to her pressure was something that genuinely shocked her internally, though she showed absolutely nothing on her composed exterior.
A human resisting my Archon-rank aura manifestation? That shouldn’t be possible unless...
Leon looked directly at her and said calmly, his voice steady despite the circumstances:
"Alright."
He deliberately lowered his glowing sword and consciously retracted his Holy energy back into his golden heart, the brilliant radiance dimming gradually.
SHIMMER... FADE...
Finally, FINALLY, I can talk to someone who speaks my language like a normal human. Everything has been complete chaos since the moment I arrived in this cursed world.
His tone sharpened noticeably as he added:
"Let’s talk and see if it was really misunderstood as you said."
Because to Leon, this was clear as day that the man behind her on his knees was his enemy.
But Leon decided to talk because she could mainly speak his language, and she felt tremendously strong, and her power was unknown as to how she made everyone kneel before her, excluding him.

He feels it.
He knows this is serious now.
In the man’s hand materialized a full-length red sword with intricate golden markings running along its blade—clearly a weapon of exceptional quality.
Leon decided to try something on instinct.
He stretched out his right hand and thought strongly about his weapon.
Come to me.
WHOOSH!
It worked immediately.
Leon felt his sword’s emotion—its eagerness, its loyalty—and he called, and it came flying to him across the arena.
Into his palm arrived his epic-ranked sword, which had previously appeared as a high-quality black blade.
But now, the moment it came into contact with his tremendous Holy energy...
SHIMMER!
TREMBLE!
GLOW!
The sword started vibrating intensely, then began absorbing his Holy energy like an endless, bottomless well—drinking in the power greedily.
Take what you need.
I have plenty.
Leon didn’t stop the flow.
He had accumulated far too much Holy energy inside himself over the months and years it had been building, generated continuously by his unknown believers across dimensions.
The sword’s appearance transformed completely, taking on a brilliant, glowing golden-white color that pulsed with divine radiance.
Leon’s palm tingled, almost burning, as the sword drank deeper, pulsing in sync with his heart.
GLOW!
SHIMMER!
RADIATE!
Leon felt its enhanced power in his hand—it felt like an entirely different weapon from before, elevated to a new tier of existence.
This is incredible.
The synergy is perfect.
He wasn’t alone in recognizing the danger.
The Vice Chief was also staring at Leon’s transformed sword with visible caution and concern, clearly realizing the genuine threat it represented.
He knows.
Smart man.

Leon’s mystical eyes—in which a golden circle had appeared around each iris, spinning rapidly like mechanical gears—locked onto the man with an eager smile, ready to test his newfound power by trying to kill this bastard.
Let’s see what you’re really made of.
However, before both their swords could clash and cause absolute devastation to everything around them in the arena—
A massive shadow suddenly covered the entire arena, blocking out the red sun above.
WHOOOOSH!
A sudden drop in temperature swept the arena as the red sun disappeared, replaced by the eerie shade of the new arrival’s presence.
A visible sigh of relief escaped from the Vice Chief’s mouth.
"Vel’kresh..."
And then, moving like a streak of pure red light—causing no collateral damage or devastation despite the incredible speed—someone appeared between them.
FWOOSH!
She was hovering slightly above the red arena floor.
Her two hands, transformed into red diamond-like crystalline claws of enormous power, caught both weapons simultaneously—Leon’s glowing Holy sword and the Vice Chief’s red blade with golden marking.
A metallic screech sang between her palms as both blades strained against her unmoving claws, the air itself warping from the pressure.
CATCH!
GRIP!

A shockwave was created from the interception, but a protective shield materialized instantly around all three of them, completely encasing them in a translucent red barrier and preventing any damage from spreading to the audience or arena.
SHIMMER!
SEAL!
What?!
Who—?!
It was a new, unexpected arrival.
But Leon was not scared or intimidated by her overwhelming presence, despite feeling the absolutely massive pressure radiating from her body like a physical weight.
Another powerful enemy?
Fine.
I’ll face them all.
He increased the rate of his Holy energy enhancement dramatically, reaching one hundred percent augmentation of his sealed baseline strength.
WHOOOOSH!
CRACKLE!
GLOW!
His aura blazed even more brilliantly than before, the golden-white radiance intensifying to near-blinding levels.
SIZZLE!
CRACK!
A distinct sizzling sound came from her crystalline red armored hand where it gripped his Holy-infused sword, the divine energy clearly affecting even her defensive technique.
She feels it.
Good.
The woman—with glowing hair like liquid fire and golden-marked eyes set in her regal crimson form—hovered slightly above the ground.
She felt his increased power surging against her grip.
Strong human
The Vice Chief standing nearby was genuinely shocked now, his eyes going wide at witnessing the human brazenness and strength against thier leaders, seeing the smoke from her crystalline hand.
Impossible!
No one resists HER presence!

chapters.title: Chapter 365: New Findings
paragraphs: She said "Good" with a visibly relieved look on her face.
I don’t want to fight this human. He’s far too strong and would be a valuable addition to our army instead of an enemy.
She was already calculating. He was likely stranded here through the portal. If that was the case, he would eventually have to fight alongside them whether he wanted to or not.
We need every warrior we can get. Especially ones this powerful.
Then she turned and spoke firmly to the Vice Chief—her brother-in-law—looking sternly at him with clear disapproval and authority in her gaze.
If I hadn’t intervened, this powerful human could have destroyed everything. I’ll have to punish him no matter who he is to me.
She knew it would be hard for him to accept punishment right now, given his pride and position, and most importantly, how badly he was dealing with her loss.

But that wouldn’t make her go easy on him for such a catastrophically huge mistake. He had to move on soon; every day their people die, he can’t be stuck in loss. She knows how he feels, but they have to deal with the reality.
He nearly jeopardized the safety of our last remaining clan. That’s unforgivable, family or not.

As she began speaking and flying upward toward the sky high above the arena, Leon noticed something massive blocking out the sun—a huge shape in red and yellow colors covering the entire open-topped arena from above.
What is that? It’s enormous.
But then Leon felt it moving. With a tremendous gust of wind that shook the entire structure, the shape flew higher into the sky.
WHOOOOOOSH! FLAP!

This revealed a truly giant flying creature beneath—it was impossibly large and utterly majestic in appearance. It looked somewhat similar to a falcon in basic structure, but was covered in brilliant red and yellow plumage that seemed to shimmer with inner fire.
I can’t believe my eyes. That thing is so big and... beautiful. And definitely not weak at all.

They flew close to the majestic creature and landed gracefully on top of its massive back, which was easily the size of a large building. Leon stood there along with the mysterious woman and the same man, whom he still didn’t like even a single bit.
I don’t care if we’re talking now. I still hate this bastard.
Suddenly, all three of them turned simultaneously to look toward the side and down.
It was Crimson—flying desperately toward them on herself, fighting against the absolutely huge, thunderous wind pressure generated by each powerful flap of the majestic creature’s enormous wings.
WHOOOOSH! STRUGGLE!
She’s having trouble. That wind is too much for her.

Leon, noticing her struggling immediately, quickly activated his Holy energy enhancement again. Then he launched himself over to her position and carefully guided her back to their location by carrying her securely in his arms.
WHOOSH! CATCH!
Her skin smelled faintly of scorched flowers and sweat—fresh from the battle.
As he gently set her down on the stable back of the giant creature, she seemed slightly startled by the sudden assistance but didn’t appear to mind at all how he’d carried her there.

Leon had done that because he could clearly see she was genuinely struggling to ascend due to the overwhelming wind pressure. He also felt instinctively that she would have gotten into serious trouble for even attempting to come up here, considering she was definitely far below these two in both raw strength and official authority.
She shouldn’t even be here. But she came anyway.
The hateful man and the Archon leader were both watching this interaction unfold with different expressions.
Some tactical ideas were forming in the Archon woman’s calculating mind as she observed their dynamic.
Interesting. Very interesting indeed.
Meanwhile, the Vice Chief seemed visibly displeased with the friendly exchange, his jaw tightening.
Too close. I don’t like this.

As the massive creature finally took off properly, heading somewhere with powerful wing strokes, the very first thing Crimson did was frantically start touching all over Leon’s body—checking his arms, his chest, his sides.
TOUCH! PAT! EXAMINE!
Her fingers pressed lightly over where once old wounds were, but he felt no pain. Only her warmth.

In Crimson’s worried mind, she had witnessed him sustain far too many life-threatening injuries during the brutal fight. She desperately wanted to confirm with her own hands that he was genuinely alright now.
Did he really recover completely from those wounds? I saw bones broken, organs damaged, and part of the body destroyed. How is that possible?
It was regeneration on a scale she had never witnessed before in her entire life. She needed to verify it herself, to believe it was real.
Leon, seeing and understanding exactly what she was doing through her concerned expression and methodical checking, allowed her to continue while smiling slightly.
She cares so much. That’s... nice, actually.
She was a complete stranger, but Leon was starting to like her.
However, after she finished her thorough examination and seemed satisfied he was truly healed, she quickly walked up to the same man Leon still harbored deep hatred for.
They immediately began talking rapidly in their own harsh language, which Leon couldn’t understand at all.
"Vel’kresh mandor sikara tor! Kala vel MANDOR sikth!" Crimson said angrily, gesturing sharply.
[You shouldn’t have stubbornly decided on that stupid trial! Father, you nearly caused a disaster, and if something happened to him, I would have never forgiven you.]
"Ira, vel kresh—" the Vice Chief began defensively.
[Ira, I was only—]
"TOR KALA VEL! Mandor sikara kresh vel’thor sikth mandor!" she interrupted, her voice rising.
[NO! This could have destroyed everything! You risked our entire future and the past!]
The man went silent after those words and could only hear her complain with his head low.
Leon didn’t understand the actual words, but he could definitely tell from her sharp tone and aggressive body language that she was genuinely angry with the man.
She’s chewing him out. Good.
But this time, surprisingly, the same man who had behaved so authoritatively and dominantly before seemed genuinely tame and submissive—like a scolded child rather than a powerful leader.
He’s... he’s actually taking it? From her?
One thing Leon now understood with certainty: Crimson and this man definitely had some kind of close familial relation.
Family, or could be something else, but that explains the familiarity.

Because when he’d seen her struggling to reach the creature’s back, Leon had realized she wasn’t nearly as strong as her earlier display had suggested. She was an Ascendant rank—powerful by normal standards, but nowhere near these two.
So how did she withstand that pressure before, when I collapsed on the ground?

He was genuinely confused about how she seemed to blow away his earlier assessment of her power. When the hateful man had released his aura and forced him to the ground, Crimson had remained standing.
But it seems now, looking back... she simply wasn’t targeted by that oppressive force. She was excluded deliberately.
It was becoming clearer to Leon that there had likely been significant misunderstandings due to the complete language barrier between them.
Communication is everything. Without it, everything goes wrong.
But Leon remained unconvinced about the "misunderstanding" explanation, because Crimson had very clearly communicated through gestures that he would die if he lost the fight.
That throat-cutting gesture was universal. That much I’m certain of.
Crimson finished her scolding and walked back toward Leon. He immediately tried communicating with her through hand signals, asking what she had just discussed with the Vice Chief.
What did you say? What did he say? Tell me!
However, before she could attempt any response, the giant creature suddenly descended and landed somewhere.
WHOOSH! THUD!

Leon heard the other woman’s commanding voice—the Archon. Now that he looked at her more carefully and closely, she appeared quite similar to Crimson in facial features. Not identical, but definitely related.
Sisters? Cousins?
Was that the reason the man was so cautious not to target her with his Aura before?
It all makes sense to Leon now.
