chapters.title: Chapter 381: Counting Ceremony—2
paragraphs: Leon was slightly surprised by how Archon Vyrra had suddenly called him out without warning to initiate this ceremonial counting.
Starting with me? Interesting choice.
He stood gracefully from his frozen seat and, with just a focused thought, emptied the monster cores he’d harvested directly from his inventory storage into physical space.
SHIMMER! APPEAR! CASCADE!

Hundreds upon hundreds of cores in different vivid colors and varying sizes materialized instantly, floating suspended in the air through his precise mana control—creating a mesmerizing display like a constellation of captured stars.
GLOW! FLOAT! SHIMMER!
He gently allowed them to descend, forming an enormous pile on the top giant stair where he’d been sitting—the sheer quantity was visually overwhelming.
CLATTER! PILE! STACK!
Leon already knew the exact number from his systematic counting during harvest.
He announced clearly to the assembled crowd, just as Archon Vyrra had instructed:
"In total, I personally eliminated 1,124 monsters. Including Ira’s contribution—she killed 131 monsters independently—our unit’s combined total comes to 1,255."
As his final words left his mouth and echoed across the arena, the entire atmosphere became utterly silent except for shocked gasps erupting periodically from various sections of the crowd.
Even the air felt still for a moment—like the city itself was holding its breath
GASP! "Impossible!" GASP! "Over a thousand?!"

During any battle, it was always life-or-death intensity—warriors were too focused on survival to accurately track anyone else’s individual performance. Some had heard rumors about how powerful this outsider was, but this?
He’s literally shattered the record for any counting ceremony in our entire documented history.
The previous highest kill count ever officially recorded was 979—achieved by a warrior whose identity had been lost to time, becoming almost mythological.
We don’t even know which legendary fighter created that benchmark anymore.

It had stood as their unbreakable record for generations. Archon Vyrra herself had declared that number as the goal for all warriors to aspire toward, giving everyone a seemingly absurd target to chase.
And he just exceeded it by over a hundred kills. Effortlessly.

After Leon’s stunning revelation, one after another, the other unit leaders began announcing their numbers—primarily reporting their personal leader’s highest individual kill count, since the ceremony’s exemption depended on a single warrior’s achievement within each unit.
"Southwest unit! Leader Kelthara—431 kills!"
"Eastern defensive line! Leader Morvan—512 kills!"
"Northern perimeter! Leader—"
The announcements continued systematically.
The highest count besides Leon was an impressive 676, achieved by Korvek—Ira’s father and the clan’s Vice Chief.
MURMUR! WHISPER! DISCUSS!

The perception of this outsider in many people’s minds had fundamentally transformed in that moment. They collectively realized with absolute clarity that he was probably the second strongest individual in their entire civilization, surpassed only by their legendary Archon herself—and potentially even stronger than Korvek, the Vice Chief.
He’s not just strong. He’s exceptional. Generational.
Most Pyrrhans accepted this new hierarchy immediately and without resentment, solely because of his undeniable demonstrated strength.
Strength is what matters. He’s proven himself beyond question.
Rumors had circulated that he was powerful, yes. But this concrete evidence was something else entirely—impossible to dismiss or downplay.
After all unit announcements concluded, Archon Vyrra made the formal declaration:
"Leon is declared the winner of this ceremonial counting! As per our ancient tradition maintained through every such ceremony, his unit’s resource tax obligation is completely waived today!"
Her voice carried across the arena with supernatural amplification.
Approximately ninety percent of the assembled warriors erupted in genuine cheers for the announcement, celebrating the record-breaking achievement.
"LEON! LEON! LEON!"
CHEER! ROAR! APPLAUD!
The remaining ten percent—those who still harbored resentment from the arena humiliation or simply disliked outsiders—remained pointedly silent, but didn’t openly object.
After the official ceremony concluded, significant activity immediately began throughout the arena and the surrounding city.

Lots of people started moving with a clear purpose—monster corpses were being systematically transported for final processing, materials were being distributed to appropriate craftsmen and storage facilities.
MOVE! HAUL! ORGANIZE!
Along with all this purposeful activity, the soft rhythmic humming of ceremonial drums began playing in the background, creating an ambient soundtrack.
HUMMM... BOOM... HUMMM... BOOM...
Everything felt synchronized, as if the entire city was moving and breathing to a shared rhythm.
This is more than logistics. It’s almost ritualistic.
Everyone appeared genuinely happy—the overall mood had shifted dramatically to something festive and celebratory rather than the grim focus of warfare.
Elaborate preparations were clearly being made for something significant.
The whole city is participating in whatever this celebration is.
Leon, however, had spotted someone departing the arena in considerable hurry during the announcement commotion—and he’d recognized that person immediately.
The hammer warrior. And she’s with the woman I fought. They’re leaving together, quickly.
He decided to follow them discreetly.
Something’s wrong. Their body language screams urgency.
Leon was just about to depart when Ira’s concerned voice stopped him:
"Where are you going, Leon? The victory celebration hasn’t happened yet. It’ll start in approximately an hour."
Her voice became slightly more meek and vulnerable at the end as she added:
"I... I wanted you to be with me during the festival celebration. I’d like to celebrate this victory together."
With me specifically. She’s asking me to be with her during the celebration.
Leon replied with a small, genuine smile spreading across his face. The fact that she clearly wanted to spend the celebration with him was honestly quite endearing.
That’s so cute of her.
"Don’t worry at all. I’ll definitely be back within just a few minutes. I promise."
Ira wanted desperately to say she’d accompany him—her mouth even opened to volunteer—but that seemed far too clingy and presumptuous given the circumstances.
I have no legitimate reason to follow him right now. It was already embarrassing enough that I basically just invited him to be my festival partner! What has gotten into me!
So she reluctantly let him go with a small nod and a firm reminder:
"You absolutely should not be late. Promise me."
Leon promised sincerely, then departed.
He flew rapidly through the red sky using his mana and various elemental powers for propulsion and control—but deliberately not activating his Holy transformation form yet.
As he left the arena’s immediate vicinity and entered the city proper, tracking his targets became more difficult due to their speed.
They’re moving fast. Really fast.
The wind screamed past his ears as he weaved through rising thermals. The scent of scorched stone and celebration fires drifted below.
Leon had to tap into his Holy power for enhanced perception—because the hammer woman was traveling at velocities where she became barely visible even to his enhanced senses.
There. Got them.
There they were—darting into a shadowed corridor, far from the main thoroughfare. Something was definitely wrong.

"LEON!
LEON!
LEON!"
CHEER!
ROAR!
APPLAUD!
The remaining ten percent—those who still harbored resentment from the arena humiliation or simply disliked outsiders—remained pointedly silent, but didn’t openly object.
After the official ceremony concluded, significant activity immediately began throughout the arena and the surrounding city.

Lots of people started moving with a clear purpose—monster corpses were being systematically transported for final processing, materials were being distributed to appropriate craftsmen and storage facilities.
MOVE!
HAUL!
ORGANIZE!
Along with all this purposeful activity, the soft rhythmic humming of ceremonial drums began playing in the background, creating an ambient soundtrack.
HUMMM...
BOOM...
HUMMM...
BOOM...
Everything felt synchronized, as if the entire city was moving and breathing to a shared rhythm.
This is more than logistics.
It’s almost ritualistic.
Everyone appeared genuinely happy—the overall mood had shifted dramatically to something festive and celebratory rather than the grim focus of warfare.
Elaborate preparations were clearly being made for something significant.
The whole city is participating in whatever this celebration is.
Leon, however, had spotted someone departing the arena in considerable hurry during the announcement commotion—and he’d recognized that person immediately.
The hammer warrior.
And she’s with the woman I fought.
They’re leaving together, quickly.
He decided to follow them discreetly.
Something’s wrong.
Their body language screams urgency.
Leon was just about to depart when Ira’s concerned voice stopped him:
"Where are you going, Leon?
The victory celebration hasn’t happened yet.
It’ll start in approximately an hour."
Her voice became slightly more meek and vulnerable at the end as she added:
I wanted you to be with me during the festival celebration.
I’d like to celebrate this victory together."
With me specifically.
She’s asking me to be with her during the celebration.
Leon replied with a small, genuine smile spreading across his face.
The fact that she clearly wanted to spend the celebration with him was honestly quite endearing.
That’s so cute of her.
"Don’t worry at all.
I’ll definitely be back within just a few minutes.
I promise."
Ira wanted desperately to say she’d accompany him—her mouth even opened to volunteer—but that seemed far too clingy and presumptuous given the circumstances.
I have no legitimate reason to follow him right now.
It was already embarrassing enough that I basically just invited him to be my festival partner!
What has gotten into me!
So she reluctantly let him go with a small nod and a firm reminder:
"You absolutely should not be late.
Promise me."
Leon promised sincerely, then departed.
He flew rapidly through the red sky using his mana and various elemental powers for propulsion and control—but deliberately not activating his Holy transformation form yet.
As he left the arena’s immediate vicinity and entered the city proper, tracking his targets became more difficult due to their speed.
They’re moving fast.
Really fast.
The wind screamed past his ears as he weaved through rising thermals.
The scent of scorched stone and celebration fires drifted below.
Leon had to tap into his Holy power for enhanced perception—because the hammer woman was traveling at velocities where she became barely visible even to his enhanced senses.
There.
Got them.
There they were—darting into a shadowed corridor, far from the main thoroughfare.
Something was definitely wrong.

chapters.title: Chapter 382: Celebration Ahead
paragraphs: Leon followed carefully as the two women entered a large dwelling constructed in the distinctive Pyrrhan architectural style—all carved stone and fire-resistant materials.
Leon entered silently immediately after them through the main entrance.
"Oh—"
CATCH! GRIP!
Leon casually caught the giant warhammer aimed directly at his head with just one hand, stopping its momentum completely.
"Easy there. I’m not here to hurt anyone."

He spoke calmly while looking directly at the tall, muscular, red-haired woman with intense crimson eyes—the hammer wielder he’d seen reporting to Archon Vyrra earlier. Behind her stood the smaller woman he’d personally fought and defeated in the arena, gripping her massive greatsword defensively.
She’s terrified.
Her eyes showed profound fear despite her weapon blazing with intensely condensed fire energy, flames wreathing the blade.
CRACKLE! BURN! GLOW!
The hammer woman’s voice came out sharp and aggressive:
"Why are you following us?! What do you want?!"
Leon answered while his attention remained focused on the massive creature lying in the middle of the room’s floor—covered comprehensively in bloody bandages from head to toe, barely breathing.
WHEEZE... GRUNT... RASP...
It’s dying. Maybe a couple of hours left at most, based on the blood loss and breathing pattern.
The creature’s labored grunts and heavy, rattling breathing were ever-present, filling the tense silence.

There was one additional person present—someone who appeared to be some sort of medic or healer based on their blood-stained robes and the medical supplies scattered around. This person immediately fled in panic to a different room upon seeing him enter and how it quickly escalated.
Not my concern.
Leon had absolutely no time to provide lengthy explanations or engage in extended conversation. He wanted to return quickly and continue training in his dimensional realm.
I’m still not even close to achieving Level 1 Holy Aura manifestation. Need more practice. Much more.
He nonchalantly waved dismissively at the hammer with his free hand—
WHOOSH! FLING!
—which resulted in the weapon being torn from her grip and clattering loudly against the far wall.
CLANG! CRASH!
Before either woman could properly react, Leon arrived directly in front of the dying creature in a blinking instant.
FWOOSH!
Neither warrior was able to fully track his movement due to his overwhelming speed advantage.
The smaller woman with the greatsword shrieked in absolute terror, tears immediately visible streaming down her face as she witnessed him disappear and reappear:
"PLEASE DON’T KILL MY ZILO!!!"
It was a desperate, heart-wrenching plea born from complete helplessness.
They think I’m here to finish it off. Understandable assumption, seeing how terrified she is.

Leon didn’t bother switching back to regular mana for this task. He simply used his Holy energy directly as he’d been practicing extensively—and also pragmatically because both women behind him might attack reflexively if they saw an opening, potentially forcing him to hurt them accidentally.
Safer this way. Faster too.
He channeled pure Holy energy directly into the dying creature’s broken body, just as he’d done countless times during his recent dimensional realm training sessions with himself as the test subject.
SHIMMER! GLOW! FLOW!
Healing was critically important for sustained combat capability. Holy energy wasn’t quite as specialized as pure Life elemental energy for medical applications, true.
Life elements can regrow entire severed limbs and organs. Holy can’t replicate that feat.
The fundamental limitation was that Holy energy couldn’t perform miraculous regeneration of completely lost body parts like Life element could.
But it’s extremely fast for everything else. And that speed matters.

However, for reattaching damaged limbs, closing wounds, purifying toxins, and accelerating natural healing processes? Holy energy was nearly equal to Life element in effectiveness, just with different applications.
Fast battlefield healing. That’s the advantage.
The massive creature began glowing brilliantly, enveloped completely in golden-white divine energy, while barely conscious.
GLOW! SHIMMER! PULSE!
Its wounds started healing at supernatural speed, flesh knitting and bones setting audibly behind his bandaged body.
CRACK! HEAL! RESTORE!
Leon immediately departed through the roof, his momentum creating a massive flash and leaving a perfectly circular hole in the stone structure.
CRASH! BOOM! WHOOOOSH!
Done. It’ll live now and even regrow that severed claw eventually.
Leon was gone, vanishing into the red sky.
The two women rushed frantically to stand beside their companion. The smaller warrior looked absolutely terrified, seeing her beloved beast still glowing with that strange, unknown energy.
Tears streamed freely down her face as she muttered desperately:
"What did he do?! Ahhhh, no! Please be okay!"
The hammer-wielding woman wanted desperately to pursue that outsider, glaring at the sky with seething anger burning in her chest.
I’ll make him pay for this intrusion! For threatening—
But she felt her complete powerlessness acutely, knowing pursuit would be utterly futile.
I can’t catch him. Can’t fight him. Can’t do anything.
Her friend’s desperate crying felt like repeated stabs directly into her heart.
She opened her mouth to swear revenge, to make some kind of oath—
I’ll tear the sky apart if I have to.
But suddenly, completely unexpected laughter was heard, cutting through the tension.
It was her friend’s voice—but joyful rather than anguished.
She looked down in shock:
"Zilo! You opened your eyes!! Your wounds are—they’re closing!"
The companion creature made happy bird-like noises, responding affectionately to its bonded partner.
CHIRP! SCREECH! PURR!
The woman with the hammer noticed the miraculous transformation occurring before her eyes.
What... what just happened? Did he... heal Zilo? But why?
Leon arrived back at the arena within minutes, landing smoothly.
He returned directly to where he’d been sitting before. Ira remained comfortably seated on the ice throne he’d created for her earlier.
Good. She waited.
Of course, the frozen seat hadn’t melted despite the oppressive heat and hours of exposure—Leon had infused it with his condensed Aura specifically to maintain structural integrity.
It wouldn’t be very impressive if my ice throne just melted into a puddle, would it?
He took his seat beside her casually.
Ira asked with genuine curiosity:
"What did you need to do? You weren’t even gone five minutes."
Leon simply waved his hand dismissively:
"Nothing particularly special. Just something minor I needed to handle."
Ira accepted this vague explanation and stopped questioning, assuming it genuinely wasn’t important.

Maybe he just wanted to take a solitary walk. He’s trapped here, away from his home and world. I can’t forget that reality. I feel terrible for him; my sister might be the same somewhere else out there.
However, one observation kept circulating in her mind:
He does look quite noticeably cheerful after returning. Almost... relieved?
Leon closed his mystical eyes, preparing to return to his dimensional realm to continue intensive training on his Holy element manifestation.
But his mind was filled with happiness and profound relief:
It worked! The portal access to my dimensional realm still functions perfectly, even in this sealed realm! Finally, I don’t have to worry about being completely cut off!
Without conscious effort, his awareness smoothly entered the dimensional realm once more.
SHIMMER! SHIFT! ENTER!

chapters.title: Chapter 383: Enjoying the festival together
paragraphs: After a short period of time—at least from the perspective of the outside world—Leon felt a gentle nudge on his shoulder, which prompted him to open his eyes.
It seems the celebration is about to start.

He’d been constantly aware of the activities happening in the external world around his physical body, but he’d deliberately been ignoring everything to maintain complete focus on his intensive training inside the dimensional realm.
Almost there. I can feel it. Soon, I’ll reach Rank 1 Aura manifestation in Holy affinity.
The breakthrough was tantalizingly close.
Leon looked directly into Ira’s crimson eyes and asked, though he already sensed the answer from the shift in atmospheric energy:
"Is it about to start?"
He knew the answer even before she responded. The entire area was now filled with the enticing aroma of delicious food—roasting meat, exotic spices, fermented drinks.
That smell is incredible.

He also noticed immediately that Ira’s hairstyle had changed dramatically during his meditation. Her hair had been flowing freely and loose before, but now it was arranged in an elaborate, well-intentioned style—pulled back elegantly with intricate braiding around her neck, some strands artfully tucked while others cascaded down.
Such a simple change, but it makes her look even more beautiful than before.
The transformation was striking.
Ira answered hurriedly, almost frantically:
"Yes! Let’s quickly get down—everyone’s waiting!"
She seemed genuinely anxious about their timing.

Leon understood why immediately. Everyone else was now assembled below on the arena ground floor, including Archon Vyrra herself. When he shifted his gaze outward toward the surrounding city, he could see Pyrrhans everywhere outside their dwellings.
The entire civilization is participating.

The atmosphere was purely festive and joyful. There was food everywhere—massive chunks of monster meat sizzling on their special racial flames, along with various kinds of drinks displayed on countless tables.
This is a major celebration. Not just a small gathering.
But first, before moving, Leon felt compelled to acknowledge what he’d noticed.
He spoke sincerely:
"Ira, you look absolutely gorgeous. That hairstyle suits you perfectly."
His compliment was genuine and heartfelt.
Though he still privately thought her clothing was far too revealing and short for his taste—something he might have to address later.
But it does seem to be deeply cultural in their clan. Everyone dresses like this—including Archon Vyrra herself.
And the men universally kept their upper bodies completely bare, which seemed equally standard.
Cultural norms. Have to respect them.
His unexpected compliment visibly startled Ira, her eyes widening.
GASP!
The urgency she’d been projecting wavered noticeably, replaced by flustered uncertainty.
She replied meekly, her voice much softer:
"Let’s... let’s quickly get down, Leon. Aunt and others are especially waiting for us, specifically."
Her emphasis on "us" carried weight.
Her words made Leon look down at the arena floor again. He noticed Archon Vyrra was indeed looking up directly at both him and Ira.
She’s watching us. Waiting.
However, Vyrra appeared quite relaxed and definitely not impatient or annoyed—she simply seemed to be deliberately waiting for them both to join before officially beginning.
We’re guests of honor, apparently.
So without further delay, Leon said:
"Let’s go down then."
Both of them jumped simultaneously from the high stair, their bodies falling through the air.
WHOOSH!

Before hitting the hard ground, each slowed themselves using their respective techniques—Leon with compressed air and light manipulation, Ira with her fire propulsion—and both landed gracefully without impact.
TAP! TAP!

One practical thing Leon genuinely appreciated was the fact that the women of this clan wore proper undergarments—panties at the very least—beneath their minimal clothing, as for the bra, he had too close an experience to say that confidence that they don’t.
Or it would be far too much exposure with their short garments. That would be uncomfortable for me to act in such a scenario.
He’d specifically noticed this detail during his intense fight with the greatsword-wielding woman in the arena, when various acrobatic movements had occurred.
Thank goodness for small mercies.
After they joined the assembled crowd, both Leon and Ira were immediately handed ceremonial glasses filled with some kind of slightly purplish liquid that shimmered in the firelight.
HAND! RECEIVE!

The gathered Pyrrhans had formed an enormous circle. In the center burned a massive bonfire constructed from their special racial flames—those distinctive red fires Leon had seen Archon Vyrra and others utilize.
CRACKLE! ROAR! BURN!
That red fire... it reminds me distinctly of Archon Vyrra’s technique.
They all possessed this special flame, though Leon could instinctively tell by simply feeling the energy signatures that not all of these fires were identical in quality or power.
Different mastery levels. Different refinement.
Suspended above the central bonfire were gigantic chunks of monster meat, sizzling and dripping fat that created aromatic smoke, filling the entire area with mouthwatering scent.
SIZZLE! DRIP! SMOKE!
Then, with a deliberate signal from Archon Vyrra, ceremonial drums and other types of musical instruments began playing in beautiful, harmonious coordination.
BOOM! STRUM! CHIME! HARMONY!
Leon could see the musicians positioned around the circle, playing with practiced skill and obvious reverence.
This is ritualistic. Important to their culture.
The music was genuinely melodious and moving.
Then, as one unified voice, everyone began singing a traditional song—clearly something deeply meaningful to their people:
"From flames we rise,
to flames we fall,
In fire’s embrace,
We give our all.
Each dawn we fight,
each dusk we stand, Pyrrhan blood, Pyrrhan land.
We survive, we live, we never yield,
Our strength, our honor, flame our shield."
Leon was genuinely surprised by the coordinated song, seeing absolutely everyone participating—from the youngest children to the oldest elders, all singing in perfect unison.
This is their anthem. Their identity.
Moved by the moment and the spirit of community, he joined in, lending his voice to theirs despite just learning the words.
Ira was singing beside him, but Leon noticed she kept glancing repeatedly at his hand for some reason, her attention obviously divided.
What is she looking at?
He was confused for a moment, then suddenly noticed a significant detail he’d initially missed:
Quite a lot of Pyrrhan couples—men and women paired together—were holding each other’s hands intimately, their fingers intertwined in the traditional gesture of partnership.
Oh. That’s the custom. Nearly eighty percent of them are holding hands; they sure are a romantic bunch.
Understanding immediately what Ira had been hoping for, Leon swiftly and smoothly switched the ceremonial glass to his other hand.
SWITCH!
Using his now-empty hand, he reached over and grasped Ira’s hand intimately, just like the other couples around them, their fingers naturally intertwining together.
HOLD! INTERTWINE!
He felt absolutely no resistance from her—her hand was warm and fit perfectly with his.
She wanted this. Good.
He then deliberately looked directly at her face, meeting her crimson eyes with his own mystical heterochromatic gaze.
She seemed to have completely frozen, her body going rigid.
She’s shocked. Adorably shocked.
She had stopped singing entirely, her mouth slightly open.
She appeared far too stunned to continue participating, her mind clearly racing.
Leon gently squeezed her hand—the one he was holding—trying to bring her back from her trance.
SQUEEZE!

She came back to awareness with a visible start, though her mind kept going blank repeatedly, her thoughts obviously consumed entirely by the fact that he was holding her hand in this specific, culturally significant way.
Only she knows what this means to her people, and she was shocked by the suddenness of everything.

Using his now-empty hand, he reached over and grasped Ira’s hand intimately, just like the other couples around them, their fingers naturally intertwining together.
HOLD!
INTERTWINE!
He felt absolutely no resistance from her—her hand was warm and fit perfectly with his.
She wanted this.
Good.
He then deliberately looked directly at her face, meeting her crimson eyes with his own mystical heterochromatic gaze.
She seemed to have completely frozen, her body going rigid.
She’s shocked.
Adorably shocked.
She had stopped singing entirely, her mouth slightly open.
She appeared far too stunned to continue participating, her mind clearly racing.
Leon gently squeezed her hand—the one he was holding—trying to bring her back from her trance.
SQUEEZE!

She came back to awareness with a visible start, though her mind kept going blank repeatedly, her thoughts obviously consumed entirely by the fact that he was holding her hand in this specific, culturally significant way.
Only she knows what this means to her people, and she was shocked by the suddenness of everything.

chapters.title: Chapter 384: Enjoying the festival together—2
paragraphs: Seeing Leon innocently singing the anthem, she forced herself to join back in, though she absolutely couldn’t make direct eye contact with him anymore.
This was too sudden. Such a big move on his part.
However, she’d been developing genuine feelings for Leon, so she didn’t protest or pull away.
I want this. I want him to hold my hand.
They maintained their hand-holding throughout the entire remainder of the song, their grip never wavering.
After the anthem finally ended, everyone raised their ceremonial glasses together in a unified toast:
"TO PYRRHA! TO SURVIVAL! TO STRENGTH!"
CLINK! DRINK!
And then the feast officially began in earnest.

Leon moved through the celebration with Ira, still holding her hand continuously. She hadn’t said anything to suggest he should stop, and he could feel her grip was mutual—she was holding him just as firmly as he held her.
Though she does seem notably more shy than usual. That’s endearing.
The drink they’d been given, Leon discovered through tasting, was definitely alcoholic—quite potent, actually.
Strong. Very strong.
However, the intoxicating effect lasted only a millisecond before being naturally purified and neutralized by his enhanced Divinordial physiology, or it could be his all elemental affinity.
No effect on me whatsoever.

The monster meat turned out to be genuinely delicious, which surprised Leon considerably. He’d been skeptical initially, having learned that monster flesh was typically inedible due to its corrupted, impure mana contamination.
But their special fire somehow purifies it during cooking. Makes it safe and actually enhances the flavor.
The meat had been seasoned with salt and various other spices he couldn’t identify, but the combination tasted remarkably good—rich, savory, with complex undertones.
This is actually excellent cuisine.
He ate substantial quantities, enjoying the exotic flavors.
From time to time during his eating, Leon received subtle system notifications indicating his maximum mana capacity was increasing slightly—not dramatically, but measurably.
The purified monster meat actually provides permanent stat increases. Valuable.
They continued drinking moderately between bites of food.
Some Pyrrhans had begun dancing in coordinated groups, moving to the rhythm of the ongoing music.
STOMP! SPIN!DANCE!
Leon decided spontaneously to take Ira along with him to join the dancers.
"Come. Let’s dance."
PULL! LEAD!
It was even more adorable seeing how red her face became during the entire experience, her cheeks flushed deeply.
She’s embarrassed but happy. I can tell.
Still, she maintained a faint, genuine smile on her face the entire time, clearly enjoying herself despite the self-consciousness.

The traditional dance was relatively simple in structure: one hand remained intertwined with your partner’s while the other rested on their waist, and you moved together fluidly to the rhythm of the music.
SWAY! TURN! STEP! FLOW!
Leon found the dance pleasant and intimate without being overly complex.
From the top level of the arena, faint laughter could suddenly be heard echoing down, along with a distinctly masculine grunt of disapproval, too far be heard by the celebration going down.
HAHA! GRUNT!

The person laughing was Archon Vyrra, clearly amused by something. The one grunting in obvious displeasure was Korvek—Ira’s father—who was currently holding a massive jar of strong drink and gulping it down steadily.
GULP! GULP! GULP!
Both their eyes were fixed on Leon and Ira, who were dancing together like an obvious romantic couple below.
Archon Vyrra commented aloud—ostensibly to empty air, but her voice was deliberately loud enough to easily reach Korvek, who was sitting several meters away from her:
"Our Ira is so lucky! Haha! What a fine match!"
Her tone was genuinely pleased and approving.
To which Korvek grunted even harder, his displeasure palpable:
"Let me drink in peace, sister-in-law. I don’t want to hear anything about this right now."
His voice carried profound frustration.
Archon Vyrra only laughed harder, completely unconcerned about the fact that he’d dropped all honorifics in his irritation.
He’s suffering seeing his daughter, Ira, loving the outsider. But he’ll accept it eventually.

Despite whatever her brother-in-law was going through right now, Vyrra was really loving this all. She had thought she had to do something, make a plan to set them up together; however, everything happened so naturally without her intervention. She just loves this.

Leon and Ira had eventually drifted away from the crowded main celebration area out of the arena, finding a quieter section with multiple benches arranged throughout—some sort of contemplation garden or rest area.
They were now sitting together on one such bench, still holding each other’s hands naturally.
This feels right. Comfortable.
Leon looked directly into her eyes. She seemed considerably less shy now than before, having gradually adjusted to the intimacy.
He said with deliberate mischief in his tone:
"Ira, are you not going to release my hand? You’re gripping it so passionately now."
His words were teasing, testing her reaction.
Ira, hearing his unexpected statement, stuttered in sudden panic:
"W-what?! I’m not—"
She immediately began trying to pull her hand away, genuinely worried she’d been too forward or clingy, but by now, in her hand, they were not just simple stranger no more.
He wants me to let go? But it felt so good holding hands with him—
However, Leon was smiling as he deliberately tightened his grip, preventing her escape.
GRIP! HOLD!
She couldn’t pull away at all against his strength, which was just her own mental wall, as Leon was currently weaker than her; if she tried, she could easily take her hand away.
Leon decided to shift the conversation, bringing her attention to something else he’d been genuinely curious about for quite a while now.
"Ira, what are they doing exactly? I’ve been observing that strange phenomenon for some time."
He gestured subtly with his free hand toward one of the other nearby benches where a Pyrrhan couple was sitting together.
POINT!

Both their hands were intertwined intimately, similar to how Leon and Ira were holding hands, but only one. But there was something distinctly different happening with this pair—a strange red glowing hue surrounded both their bodies, pulsing rhythmically.
GLOW! PULSE! SHIMMER!

Above them hovered a peculiar flame that appeared to be a mixture of both their individual special fires, swirling together in patterns that seemed almost alive. The flame contained an otherworldly strangeness, colors shifting and blending in ways that defied normal fire behavior.
SWIRL! MERGE! DANCE!

The couple themselves weren’t even consciously focusing on maintaining this phenomenon—it seemed to be occurring naturally, autonomously, as they sat together in intimate stillness, seemingly lost in each other.
What is that energy? It’s not just their normal racial fire. Something deeper.

This wasn’t the first time Leon had witnessed this particular phenomenon. He’d actually seen it quite frequently throughout the festival—multiple couples exhibiting the same glowing aura and merged flame manifestation.
But I never asked about it because I was too preoccupied enjoying the celebration together with her.
Now, his analytical curiosity had finally gotten the better of him.
Hearing his innocent question, Ira’s words caught abruptly in her throat.
GULP!
She remained completely silent for an extended, awkward moment—several seconds that stretched uncomfortably.
Why is she hesitating so much? Is this taboo to discuss?
Finally, she replied in an extremely meek voice, barely louder than a whisper:
"They are... they are making love."
Her words were so quiet Leon almost didn’t hear them over the distant festival music.
WHISPER...
Leon immediately understood the full meaning and cultural implication of her words.
Oh. OH. That’s what that represents; they really are a different race. The merging of their fires is... intimate. Very intimate.
Meanwhile, Ira’s internal mind was absolutely screaming in mortified panic:

WHAAAAT?! Why did he ask me THAT?! Of all the questions! Does he understand what he’s asking?! Does he know what it means that we’re sitting here alone holding hands like this?! Is he—does he want—NO! Focus! Don’t think about it! Ahhhhhh!
Her face had turned an even deeper shade of crimson than normal, visible even against her naturally red Pyrrhan skin.
FLUSH! BURN!
She couldn’t bring herself to look at Leon’s face at all, her eyes fixed firmly on the ground between her feet.
I can’t believe I just said that out loud to him!

chapters.title: Chapter 385: Leveling up
paragraphs: Leon, however, was still genuinely curious about one additional thing. She had said they were "making love" in that way—so did that mean they also created babies through that same fire-merging process?
Is their reproduction entirely different from humans’? That would make sense given their racial uniqueness.
It was sincere, innocent curiosity on his part—purely academic interest in their biology.
So he asked her directly:
"And does that method also result in children? Is that how Pyrrhans reproduce?"
For Ira, this follow-up question might have been far too much for her already overwhelmed emotional state to handle.
Ira’s hand trembled for a split second, as if her entire bloodstream had turned to boiling magma.
SNAP!
With a loud, high-pitched "YES!" that came out almost as a shriek, she abruptly pulled her hand away from his grip with surprising force—
YANK! ESCAPE!
—and then immediately launched herself into the air, flying rapidly into the distance without looking back.
WHOOOOSH!
She’s fleeing. That was definitely too much.
Leon watched as she genuinely disappeared from sight, her silhouette vanishing into the red-tinted sky.
She’s really gone.
He didn’t follow after her or attempt to call her back.
She needs time to process. I pushed too far with that question.
However, he had gotten his answer—indirect confirmation that yes, their reproductive process was indeed connected to that fire-merging phenomenon.
Alright. That’s actually fascinating from a biological standpoint.
But he also realized she’d left without collecting her share of the harvested loot from his inventory storage.
She might come back soon for that. Or tomorrow. Whenever she’s ready.
Taking a deep, centering breath, Leon refocused his attention on what he was genuinely most excited about now that Ira had departed.
I did enjoy spending time with her. But she clearly needs space and time for now, and I have important work to do.
He looked around the quiet park area carefully. There was considerable empty space available here—perfect for construction.
Should I build my residence here, or somewhere more isolated?
He briefly considered locating somewhere on a distant cliff away from the main city, similar to how Archon Vyrra’s personal dwelling was positioned in that mountain cave.
But no. Here is better. Close to the arena, central to the city. More practical.
Walking purposefully to a particularly empty clearing, Leon began using his Earth, Water, and Fire elemental control simultaneously to construct his creation.
RUMBLE! FLOW! SHAPE! HARDEN!
The earth steamed faintly under his fingers as clay compressed and hardened. The scent of scorched stone and mineral hung in the air.
The few Pyrrhan couples still occupying other benches in the park noticed his activity for a brief moment, then deliberately ignored it and returned to their romantic activities.
They recognize me. And they know I have more than enough authority to do whatever I’m doing.
The construction took approximately several focused minutes. Leon carefully built a solid ground-floor foundation for his dwelling—nothing extravagant, but well-crafted.
Not taking too much space. Five hundred square feet of land should be sufficient for now.
The structure contained one large main room and a separate shower area with proper luxuries he’d missed during travel.
He placed a comfortable bed inside from his inventory storage, along with a proper bathtub in the shower room.
Actual civilization amenities. Finally.
He also added several decorative pieces he’d been carrying—furniture and art he’d acquired from Seraphine’s castle when they’d evacuated.
Luxurious sofa, table, and wall hangings. Make it feel like a real home rather than just a shelter.
Leon appreciated having the capability to take proper baths.
That will come later, though. First and foremost—it’s time to level up.
Excitement building in his chest, Leon entered his new dwelling and took a seated position on the floor, cross-legged in meditation posture.
SETTLE! BREATHE!
From his inventory, he retrieved the core—the massive, most powerful one he possessed.
The hydra’s nearly-Archon-rank core.
SHIMMER! MATERIALIZE! GLOW!
Leon was just about to initiate the absorption process when suddenly, unbidden, a vivid flashback flashed through his mind—his Primordial Mark of Fate appearing, manipulating events, creating danger.
Wait. That cursed mark might really try to interfere with this critical advancement.
Realization crashed over him like cold water.
With this powerful core, I’m expecting to break through multiple levels from my current Level 19. This is exactly the kind of significant moment when that mark would cause problems.
He couldn’t afford to be careless like before. Not with stakes this high.
I need to be properly prepared. Take precautions.
First, Leon teleported immediately out of his brand-new residence and started flying rapidly into the distance, away from the populated city.
WHOOOOSH!
He reached ten kilometers away in minimal time.
Not far enough. If something catastrophic happens, I could still damage the city from here.
He thought for another moment, then continued flying at maximum speed.
Only after reaching a full hundred kilometers away from the Pyrrhan settlement did he finally stop and feel satisfied with the safety margin.
This should be a sufficient distance.
He chose a remote cliff face and took a seated position there, the barren landscape stretching endlessly around him.
SETTLE! FOCUS!
Then Leon opened his cosmic shop interface, needing to purchase protective items to properly prepare for whatever might come.
His fingers moved instinctively, swiping open menus only he could see. Faint hums of cosmic static danced across his fingertips with each selection
My Causality reserves have been sucked dry for so long. But today’s battle earned me a decent amount.
His total earnings today were approximately 25 million Causality.
If only I’d been able to finish that hydra myself without Archon Vyrra’s intervention. The reward would have been substantially higher.
He was also waiting for his regular monthly Causality payment from the higher beings who supported him, but that time hadn’t arrived yet.
It hasn’t been a full month since the last payment. And time inside my dimension clearly doesn’t count toward that timer—it’s a separate dimensional space, not physical reality.
He was carefully keeping track to see if there was any time dilation effect between where those higher beings are and him.
Leon purchased three critical items:
Phoenix Feather Amulet (Legendary – Item) Revives the wearer upon death, once.
Price: 2,500,000 Causality
Vendor: Resurrecto Maximus
He bought two Phoenix Feather Amulets for redundancy.
Hourglass of Reversal (Rare – Item) Rewinds time in a 3-meter radius by three seconds. Single-use.
Price: 1,200,000 Causality
Vendor: Professor Time-a-lot
I don’t know exactly what tactical use the hourglass might provide, but having a literal time-reversal option could be invaluable.

chapters.title: Chapter 386: Leveling up—2
paragraphs: Leon connected himself to one Phoenix Feather Amulet with a drop of his blood, establishing the binding.
BOND! CONNECT!
However, he discovered he wasn’t able to connect to both amulets simultaneously—apparently, there was a limitation preventing dual binding.
One active at a time. Fine.
He wore the bound amulet around his neck and kept the second one positioned immediately next to him as backup emergency insurance.
Now I have two lifelines plus a three-second time reversal option if needed.
Confidence surged through him.
I’m as prepared as I can reasonably be.
The nearly-Archon-rank core materialized fully—an enormous sphere approximately two feet in diameter, pulsing with condensed power.
GLOW! PULSE! THRUM!
Leon didn’t hesitate any longer. He initiated the absorption process, his mana making contact with the core’s surface.
TOUCH! CONNECT! FLOW!
Then, intense, overwhelming energy started flooding violently into his body like a broken dam.
His entire form took on a bright purplish-red-green hue, corresponding directly to the three primary elements the hydra had possessed: poison, fire, and Life.
GLOW! SHIMMER! PULSE!
Leon immediately tried controlling the flow rate at which the energy was entering his body—attempting to moderate and manage the influx.
Slow down! Too fast!
The feeling was euphoric but dangerously intense, with absolutely no sense of naturally slowing or stopping.
RUSH! FLOOD! OVERWHELM!
The first level-up message appeared before his eyes:
[LEVEL UP! You are now Level 20!]
Leon felt the dramatic increase in his overall strength—muscles, bones, mana pathways all simultaneously reinforcing.
Yes! But it’s not stopping—
It didn’t pause like hitting a barrier. Instead, it continued smoothly, almost like melting through butter.
After only a few seconds without additional messages, another notification appeared:
[LEVEL UP! You are now Level 21!]
Then the messages began bombarding him continuously, the euphoria filling his entire being with overwhelming sensation:
[LEVEL UP! You are now Level 22! [LEVEL UP! You are now Level 23!] [LEVEL UP! You are now Level 24!] [LEVEL UP! You are now Level 25!]
Non-stop advancement.

The level-up notifications weren’t the only changes. He was physically feeling his strength exploding exponentially—his stamina capacity, his maximum mana pool, his mental processing speed, and his intelligence stat.
I feel like I can do anything! This power is incredible!
It felt absolutely amazing—addictive, even.
Until suddenly the advancement messages stopped—but the bright multi-colored hue covering his entire body didn’t fade.
What? Why did it stop?
His core was still actively absorbing massive amounts of energy. The monster core itself was nowhere near depleted.
Leon felt something building dangerously—not just internally, but externally as well.
RUMBLE! CRACK! DARKEN!
Up in the red sky above him, massive storm clouds were rapidly forming from nothing, crackling with supernatural lightning.
Tribulation. The breakthrough tribulation to the Ascendant rank.
He quickly opened his status screen interface and glanced at his current level.
[Level 30 - Master Rank]
One level away from officially becoming Ascendant. This is the threshold test.
Leon knew instinctively he absolutely couldn’t release his Holy energy right now—it would catastrophically interfere with the elemental mana he was currently absorbing.
No idea what would happen if I mixed divine and elemental energy during tribulation. Probably nothing good.
Even so, he could distinctly feel there was at least a twenty-five percent base increase in his fundamental physical strength compared to before this absorption began.
And that’s without any enhancement techniques active.
He examined his status screen more carefully. The hollow star symbol representing his stats progression was approximately half-filled now.
Leon prepared himself for the incoming ordeal with absolutely everything available to him:
Every Aura he possessed wrapped defensively around his body in layered shields—Ice Aura, Earth Aura, Wind Aura, and every other Aura he had all at maximum intensity.
LAYER! SHIELD! PROTECT!
Every defensive skill and technique he’d learned deployed simultaneously—barriers, wards, damage reduction passives.
Every physical enhancement he could activate was engaged—toughened skin, reinforced bones, accelerated healing.
Maximum defense. Whatever’s coming, I’ll endure it.
This preparation wait wasn’t long.
CRACK! BOOM! DESCEND!
The first tribulation lightning bolt descended with a resounding, earth-shaking sound, striking directly onto his position with pinpoint accuracy.
STRIKE! IMPACT! PENETRATE!
And this entire dramatic scene was being carefully watched by two powerful individuals hovering distantly up in the sky—Archon Vyrra and Korvek, observing from a safe distance.
Archon Vyrra was smiling gleefully, her expression one of pure delight.
She commented to Korvek beside her:
"Do you still not believe your daughter is extraordinarily lucky to have caught his attention?"
In response, only heavy silence came from the Vice Chief.
He can’t deny it anymore, not after witnessing this.
Archon Vyrra continued with genuine excitement, not even looking for Korvek’s actual response:
"A new Archon is about to be born! How thrilling!"
The lightning landed as if it had completely bypassed and passed through every single defense Leon had carefully prepared—shields, barriers, Auras—all utterly ignored.
PENETRATE! STRIKE! IMPACT!
It connected directly with Leon’s actual body.
"Urrrghhh!"
The defensive shields of earth and ice constructs—everything was completely disregarded by the tribulation lightning.
What the hell?! My defenses did absolutely nothing!
The pain was significant but manageable—nothing he fundamentally couldn’t endure with his enhanced pain tolerance.
But my defenses not working at all is outrageous! How is anyone supposed to defend against this?!
However, as the initial pain receded, Leon felt profound changes happening throughout his entire being.
Wait. The lightning—while painful—is actually helping me become stronger. Changing me from within at a fundamental level.
This tribulation lightning was fundamentally different from a normal attack. It was painful, yes, but simultaneously beneficial—refining and tempering rather than purely destroying.
It’s reconstructing my body. Making it better.

Understanding this mechanism, Leon deliberately removed all his layered defenses—they weren’t providing any protection anyway, and this tribulation energy needed direct contact to properly temper him.
No point wasting mana maintaining useless shields.
The second thunderbolt descended directly onto his now-undefended body.
CRACK! STRIKE! BURN!
"Urrrgghhh!"
The pain intensified, but after it passed, he distinctly felt measurable improvement in his fundamental constitution.
Stronger. More refined.
Then the third bolt struck.
BOOM! IMPACT!
Same pattern—intense pain followed by tangible advancement.
But this time, an additional message appeared before him in the form of a golden transparent system screen:
[Do you wish to continue the tribulation to the second stage, or end the advancement here?]

BOND!
CONNECT!
However, he discovered he wasn’t able to connect to both amulets simultaneously—apparently, there was a limitation preventing dual binding.
One active at a time.
Fine.
He wore the bound amulet around his neck and kept the second one positioned immediately next to him as backup emergency insurance.
Now I have two lifelines plus a three-second time reversal option if needed.
Confidence surged through him.

chapters.title: Chapter 387: Becoming an Ascendant
paragraphs: [Do you wish to continue the tribulation to the second stage, or end the advancement here?]
A choice? I can stop now if I want.
Leon considered for only a single second before deciding firmly:
Continue. I’ll never get this opportunity again.
The fourth lightning bolt descended onto him immediately after his mental confirmation.
CRACK! STRIKE! SEAR!
"Urgh!"
This strike was noticeably more brutal than the previous ones.
His skin visibly sizzled—the first actual physical injury significant enough that his natural passive regeneration wasn’t sufficient.
Damage is exceeding my healing rate now.
He had to actively channel Life elemental energy to heal the burns as they formed.
HEAL! RESTORE! MEND!
The tribulation continued relentlessly.
The seventh thunderbolt descended with devastating force.
BOOM! STRIKE! RAVAGE!
This time, instead of just grunting despite his exceptional pain tolerance, Leon actually screamed audibly.
"AHHHHH!"
Blood poured from the corners of his mouth. His entire body was covered in severe burns, the damage reaching critical levels.
This is... this is really dangerous now.
But Leon healed himself back up almost instantaneously—his Life elemental affinity was actively working the entire time, constantly repairing damage.
GLOW! HEAL! RESTORE!
Another system message appeared:
[Do you wish to continue to the final stage of tribulation?]
Leon’s response was immediate and unwavering:
"Continue."
But then an unprecedented follow-up message appeared:
[Are you absolutely certain? The final stage has resulted in death for 90% of attempted advancements.]
What the hell? Is the system actually trying to scare me into stopping?
He can’t be mediocre; he needs to go above and beyond to live the way he wants.
Leon’s expression hardened with absolute determination.
"I said CONTINUE!"
The storm clouds above expanded dramatically—now reaching an absolutely massive scale, covering nearly one hundred kilometers of sky.
EXPAND! DARKEN! CRACKLE!
Then the eighth tribulation lightning bolt began descending—
This one was fundamentally different.
BOOM! DESCEND! ENGULF!
The lightning was thick as a building, and Leon’s entire body became completely enveloped within it—consumed by crackling energy.
He was trapped inside, screaming continuously:
"AHHHHHH!"
This tribulation was too drastically different from the previous ones.
His Life elemental healing and even his Light affinity’s restorative properties were both working at absolute maximum capacity simultaneously.
HEAL! RESTORE! BURN! DAMAGE!
His skin was sizzling, becoming charred black. Blood leaked constantly from the corners of his mouth and from wounds across his entire body.
The damage-and-heal cycle created a nightmarish loop—getting wounded, healing, then immediately destroyed again.
"AHHHHH!"
His clothes had been completely incinerated long ago—by the third strike, he’d been rendered naked.
Endure! I have to endure this!
Leon’s breathing became severely ragged as the lightning finally released him.
"Fucking... shit... that one was... too painful..."

However, he distinctly felt his body was dramatically more durable and fundamentally stronger now. His mana pathways were significantly more refined and efficient. His very essence—the fundamental nature of his being—was being elevated to a higher tier of existence.
Worth it. Despite the agony, it was worth it.
The clouds continued crackling ominously above.
CRACK! RUMBLE! CHARGE!
Leon knew immediately another strike was incoming.
Not done yet. One more.
His body became covered in a brilliant hue mixing green Life energy, bright Light element, and the three absorbed colors from the monster core’s residual power.
GLOW! SHIMMER! RADIATE!
He was burning through his mana reserves without any limitation—spending hundreds of points per second just to stay alive and heal.
One thing I’m genuinely grateful for—I can feel I have more than enough total mana capacity now. Those level-ups increased my maximum pool substantially.
The final tribulation lightning began forming—
GATHER! CONDENSE! CHARGE!
Leon’s small figure in comparison to the absolutely massive thunder column, which would soon engulf the entire area, was utterly puny.
I’m nothing compared to this force. Just a speck.
DESCEND! STRIKE! CONSUME!
"AHHHHHHHH!"
The pain was beyond anything he’d ever experienced—beyond torture, beyond the Phoenix Tears reconstruction, beyond everything.
So... painful... can’t... think...
Leon gritted his teeth so hard they cracked, enduring through sheer willpower alone.

I have to do this! I have to survive and become strong! To fight against my damned Primordial Mark of Fate! To survive and live Life on my own terms! For that, I must not just survive but become stronger than anyone else!
"AHHHHHH!"
His body, covered in catastrophic injuries across every surface, had become grotesque—barely recognizable as human.
DAMAGE! HEAL! BURN! RESTORE!
The healing was desperately trying to keep pace, but it simply wasn’t enough against this overwhelming, destructive force.
He was burning through hundreds of mana points every single second.
Don’t stop! Keep healing! Don’t give up!
The two observers hovering distantly up in the sky were holding their breath in genuine tension.
Even Korvek—who hadn’t particularly liked Leon initially—seemed to have tightened fists and appeared to be genuinely rooting for the outsider’s survival now.
Come on. You can make it, you shameless bastard.
Finally, mercifully, it ended.
FADE! DISSIPATE! SILENCE!
Leon’s eyes were bloodshot. His body was comprehensively covered in blood. His bones were even partially visible through gaps in burned flesh.
Did I... survive?
But his powerful healing regenerated everything in minimal time.
GLOW! RESTORE! HEAL!
He slumped onto the rocky ground, completely exhausted.
COLLAPSE! BREATHE!
His chest was heaving with labored breaths.
I survived. I actually survived without even needing to use the Phoenix Feather.
Relief flooded through him.
He carefully stored the two Phoenix Feather Amulets and the Hourglass of Reversal back into his inventory for future emergencies.
Saved them. Good.
A triumphant system message appeared:
[CONGRATULATIONS! You have become an ASCENDANT!]
The strength he was feeling now coursing through his body—he couldn’t adequately describe it with words.
This is... incredible. I’m fundamentally different now.
However, even after achieving Ascendant rank, the hydra’s core wasn’t finished—residual energy was still steadily entering his body.
But now Leon discovered he could actually control the flow rate properly. His mastery over mana manipulation itself had increased dramatically. Everything felt more natural and intuitive.
Complete control. Finally.
[LEVEL UP! You are now Level 31! [LEVEL UP! You are now Level 32!] [LEVEL UP! You are now Level 33! [LEVEL UP! You are now Level 34! [LEVEL UP! You are now Level 35! [LEVEL UP! You are now Level 36!]
In total, he leveled up six additional times before the massive core finally crumbled completely into worthless ash.
CRUMBLE! DUST! SCATTER!
Leon finally released a long, satisfied sigh.
"Phew. That was... a lot."
But then a wide, genuine smile spread across his face—the kind of pure joy that came from achieving something truly significant.
"But I absolutely loved every second of it!"

chapters.title: Chapter 388: Clone or Real?
paragraphs: Archon Vyrra and Korvek, who had been watching intently from high up in the sky, finally departed now that the dramatic breakthrough was complete.
WHOOSH! DEPART!
They had only remained here initially because of the massive commotion and spiritual pressure, waiting throughout the tribulation to provide emergency assistance if Leon had needed it.
But he managed it entirely on his own. Impressive.
Now that the crisis had passed successfully, they were gone.
Archon Vyrra appeared genuinely elated by what she’d witnessed, her expression bright with satisfaction.
A new Archon in our realm. And such a powerful one at that.
Even Korvek seemed visibly impressed despite his earlier reservations, nodding with grudging respect as they flew back toward the city.
The outsider has proven himself beyond question.
Leon remained lying there completely naked on the rocky ground for an extended while, his body still recovering from the ordeal despite being fully healed.
Just... need a moment. That was intense.
At the same time, he was eagerly examining his dramatically transformed status information:
[Character Information]
[Name: Prim Leo’el Divaneth]
[Level: 36]
[Class: Elemental Paragon (SSS)]
[Age: 18 (Soul Age: 34)]
[Race: Divinordial]
[Title: Hope Breaker (Common), Anomaly (Divine), Myth Breaker (Mythical)]
[Cultivation: Ascendant Rank]
[Affinity: All (Rank 7)]
[Strength: ★☆]
[Agility: ★☆]
[Stamina: ★☆]
[Intelligence: 1915]
Leon’s eyes carefully scanned through each statistic, analyzing the changes.
Strength, Agility, Stamina, Mana, and Intelligence—all of them experienced massive jumps.
He could distinctly feel the vastness of power coursing through his body right now. However, he wasn’t entirely certain exactly how strong he’d become in practical terms.
But one thing is absolutely clear—I’m many, many times stronger than before the advancement.
His base statistics— and even Mana and Intelligence—had experienced well over a one hundred percent increase. Possibly even more substantial.
Need proper testing to confirm, but probably two hundred or even three hundred percent improvement. Maybe higher.
Even without activating his Holy energy transformation, he was now a genuine force to be reckoned with.
My base form alone is formidable now.
Leon also discovered significant physical changes to his actual body structure during his examination.
His physique had become noticeably more refined—chiseled and compressed yet still distinctly muscular, with enhanced definition.
Leaner but stronger. More efficient.
And his height had increased from his previous nearly six feet four inches to now standing at six feet six inches tall.
Two inches taller. The tribulation literally made me grow.
His manhood had also received a respectful, decent enhancement in size and proportion.
Well. That’s... certainly a bonus I wasn’t expecting.
Testing his newfound control, Leon casually created a thin mirror surface using his Ice affinity.
SHIMMER! FORM! REFLECT!
The elemental energy responded far more smoothly and naturally than ever before—everything felt effortless and intuitive.
My control has improved dramatically. This is what Ascendant rank feels like.
Leon still possessed hundreds of unused monster cores remaining in his inventory from the day’s harvesting.
He experimentally withdrew just ten cores of various levels to test something specific.
MATERIALIZE! GLOW!
He absorbed them rapidly in minimal time—his enhanced control made the process smooth and efficient.
However, no level-up notifications appeared. He felt only slight, marginal improvements to his statistics.
Diminishing returns now that I’m an Ascendant rank. I’d need to continue absorbing maybe hundreds more cores just to gain a couple of additional levels.
He consciously chose to save the remaining cores for later strategic use.
Better to distribute them or use them when I actually need the boost.
Now it was time for the skill stones—the real treasure.
Leon had collected approximately thirty to forty skill stones total during the massive battle. However, frustratingly, he’d only obtained three actual technique stones among them.
The drop rate is absurdly low. It should have been significantly higher given the quantity of monsters killed.
Even the powerful hydra boss had only dropped a skill stone rather than a technique.
But what I did get is exceptional quality.
Leon started with the skill he was most genuinely excited about—the Legendary-ranked ability he’d obtained from the hydra itself.
The skill’s name was[Hydra’s Division],a legendary skill with a cloning ability that allowed him to create a duplicate of himself possessing exactly ten percent of his actual total Strength.
Ten percent doesn’t sound like much, but given my current power level, that’s still formidable.
Leon crushed the glowing skill stone between his fingers, and brilliant light immediately flowed from it directly into his temple.
CRUSH! FLOW! ABSORB!
Surprisingly, it didn’t feel even the slightest bit overwhelming or disorienting—his enhanced Intelligence stat made integration effortless.
Slight internal changes occurred throughout his body and mana pathways, accompanied by comprehensive information flooding his consciousness about the skill’s mechanics and limitations.
Interesting. Very interesting.
The ability had a restriction—he could create only one clone initially at Level 1 mastery, having just learned it.
Don’t know yet if higher mastery levels will allow multiple simultaneous clones. Need to test and develop it.
But one critical advantage he immediately appreciated: the skill had absolutely no cooldown period whatsoever.
I can dismiss and recreate it instantly if needed. That’s incredibly valuable tactically.
There was an explicit warning embedded in the skill knowledge:[Do not attempt creation without sufficient Intelligence stat—mental fracture may result.]
Good thing my Intelligence is nearly two thousand now. It should be more than adequate.
The clone would persist until either deliberately dismissed or physically destroyed through combat.
Permanent duration. Excellent for reconnaissance and multi-tasking.
Leon was extremely content with this acquisition.
Ten percent of my Strength isn’t negligible from others’ perspective. And I know exactly how tactically useful this capability will be.
He decided to test the skill immediately, confident in his substantial Intelligence statistic.
Leon activated[Hydra’s Division].
ACTIVATE! DRAIN! FLOW!
Two thousand mana points were swiftly consumed from his total reserves—a noticeable but manageable expenditure.
Then something profoundly strange began happening to his physical body.
His form appeared to literally be splitting into two separate entities—not dividing like a cell, but growing and being separated simultaneously.
SPLIT! GROW! SEPARATE!
It was genuinely not a pleasant sight to witness or experience. The process was moderately painful, though his exceptional pain tolerance allowed him to endure it by simply gritting his teeth.
GRIT! ENDURE!
The entire duplication process was completed within several seconds.
The visual result wasn’t particularly aesthetically pleasing—though notably, no actual blood was spilled during the separation.
Clean division. Good.
Standing before Leon’s original body was another perfect version of himself—identical in every physical detail. Its eyes slowly opened, looking directly at him.
OPEN! GAZE! CONNECT!
No—he was looking at himself. The mental sensation was profoundly strange and disorienting.
This is... bizarre.
The clone felt simultaneously like it was him, but he was also distinctly still himself in his original body.
Their minds were technically two separate consciousnesses, yet functionally operated as one unified intelligence.
Two bodies, one mind. Or one mind experiencing two bodies simultaneously.
Leon could observe through the clone’s perspective, but the clone could also look back at his original form—and both experiences felt like they were being conducted by a single unified person.
I can use this for surveillance and reconnaissance perfectly. See through its eyes while maintaining my own perspective.
However, the sensation was genuinely weird and took mental adjustment.
It didn’t feel like controlling a separate clone entity that might develop its own distinct personality.
We’re both versions of myself—a singular consciousness experiencing two simultaneous physical forms. Not different individuals, but two bodies with one unified mind.
Leon appreciated this design tremendously.
Much better than risking a clone developing an independent personality or potentially o betraying me.
He wasn’t worried, though, as he felt like he could dissolve it any second.
They both felt like they were one and the same entity existing in parallel.
However, Leon could still distinctly identify which body was his "original" self.
The mana core. That’s the key identifier.
He realized the fundamental difference: the original mana core in his primary body was distinct from the one present in the duplicate.
The clone possesses ten percent of my physical capabilities, but...
Leon focused his senses carefully.
It doesn’t have access to the same mana heart structure. I feel absolutely no trace of Holy energy whatsoever in this second version of myself.
That was a critical limitation to understand.
So the clone can’t access my divine power. Only my standard elemental abilities are at reduced capacity.
This skill would require extensive testing and experimentation to fully understand its tactical applications and limitations.

Leon stood there examining the naked duplicate version of himself through both sets of eyes simultaneously—his original perspective looking at the clone, while the clone’s viewpoint looked back at his primary form.
This is going to take some getting used to. But the potential is incredible.

WHOOSH!
DEPART!
They had only remained here initially because of the massive commotion and spiritual pressure, waiting throughout the tribulation to provide emergency assistance if Leon had needed it.
But he managed it entirely on his own.
Impressive.
Now that the crisis had passed successfully, they were gone.
Archon Vyrra appeared genuinely elated by what she’d witnessed, her expression bright with satisfaction.
A new Archon in our realm.
And such a powerful one at that.
Even Korvek seemed visibly impressed despite his earlier reservations, nodding with grudging respect as they flew back toward the city.
The outsider has proven himself beyond question.
Leon remained lying there completely naked on the rocky ground for an extended while, his body still recovering from the ordeal despite being fully healed.
Just... need a moment.
That was intense.

[Name: Prim Leo’el Divaneth]
[Level: 36]
[Class: Elemental Paragon (SSS)]
[Age: 18 (Soul Age: 34)]
[Race: Divinordial]
[Title: Hope Breaker (Common), Anomaly (Divine), Myth Breaker (Mythical)]
[Cultivation: Ascendant Rank]
[Affinity: All (Rank 7)]
[Strength: ★☆]
[Agility: ★☆]
[Stamina: ★☆]

But one thing is absolutely clear—I’m many, many times stronger than before the advancement.

Possibly even more substantial.

Maybe higher.
Even without activating his Holy energy transformation, he was now a genuine force to be reckoned with.
My base form alone is formidable now.

His physique had become noticeably more refined—chiseled and compressed yet still distinctly muscular, with enhanced definition.
Leaner but stronger.
More efficient.

FORM!
REFLECT!
The elemental energy responded far more smoothly and naturally than ever before—everything felt effortless and intuitive.
My control has improved dramatically.
This is what Ascendant rank feels like.

GLOW!

Diminishing returns now that I’m an Ascendant rank.

chapters.title: Chapter 389: Serious Training
paragraphs: Leon proceeded to learn several more skills from the remaining stones, selecting abilities he found genuinely useful while deliberately leaving behind the lightning elemental skill, which possessed excellent capabilities perfectly suited for Seraphine when he eventually gave it to her.
She’ll appreciate this one. Lightning affinity is her element.
The stones felt warm in his palm, almost alive with potential as he sorted through them one by one.
As for mastering other elemental techniques, Leon was confident he could learn those himself through dedicated practice rather than relying on skill stones, which have the same ability.
No need to waste these limited resources on things I can develop naturally, and elemental control also gives me more freedom.
After finishing with the skill stones, it was time for the technique stones—the truly valuable acquisitions.

There was an Epic-rank technique called [Blazing Ascension], which dramatically enhanced his physical capabilities through fire-infused body reinforcement—similar in application to his Raijin’s Descent lightning technique, which remained one of his absolute best abilities despite its rank.
Another excellent enhancement technique. These stack multiplicatively with my other buffs.
Leon crushed the crimson stone between his fingers, feeling it crumble like hot sand. Brilliant light immediately flowed from the fragments directly into his temple, warm against his skin.
CRUSH! ABSORB! INTEGRATE!
Knowledge flooded his mind—muscle memory, energy pathways, timing sequences—all slotting into place like puzzle pieces, finding their natural positions.

As for the remaining two technique stones—one was [Chain Conflagration], allowing fire attacks to jump between multiple targets, and the other was [Detonating Inferno], a powerful fire-based explosion technique with delayed trigger capability.
Good offensive options. Versatile applications.

These weren’t all the techniques Leon acquired, however. He also systematically learned the various techniques he’d previously collected and stored from the Middle Domain—specifically, the skill stones he’d confiscated from the Sixth Supreme Leader’s spatial ring during that confrontation.
Might as well make use of everything I’ve accumulated.

He spent time methodically learning numerous techniques, expanding his combat repertoire significantly. Each stone dissolved between his fingers, some feeling cool like river rocks, others hot as coals, each leaving distinct tingling sensations as knowledge integrated.
CRUSH! LEARN! INTEGRATE! REPEAT!
After completing his technique absorption, Leon was eager to conduct a critical experiment.

He and his clone both dressed in clothes retrieved from his inventory—identical outfits to avoid confusion. The fabric felt strange against his newly refined skin, somehow both familiar and different.
MATERIALIZE! DRESS!
Then Leon attempted something he’d been theorizing about: using his clone to enter the dimensional realm in conscious form while his original body remained in the physical world.
If this works, the training implications are astronomical.
He focused his will through the clone’s perspective and initiated the dimensional transition—
SHIMMER! SHIFT! SUCCESS!
It worked perfectly! The clone was now sitting cross-legged in meditation inside the dimensional realm while Leon’s original body remained seated in the Pyrrhan realm.
Incredible! This opens up entirely new possibilities.
Even more remarkable was discovering that new knowledge and skills he’d learned after the clone’s creation were also accessible to the duplicate.
Which means if it trains inside the dimension, I should benefit too. That’s the critical test.
Leon was eager to find out if this theory held true.

The sensation of simultaneously existing here in the physical world and there in the dimensional realm was profoundly disorienting. It felt like trying to focus on two conversations happening at once—possible, but requiring intense concentration.
It’ll take considerable time getting used to this split awareness. But the potential...

If this succeeded, he’d effectively be training at double speed. And inside his time dimension—which operated at one thousand times faster temporal rate—that would translate to outrageous, unprecedented speed of growth.

I’ve been accumulating new techniques, skills, and abilities constantly. But their individual levels and mastery progression? Those have been lagging severely behind. With this method, everything changes.
"Whoa..."
Leon felt it clearly after only a few minutes had passed in the outside world.

The memory and muscle memory of his clone’s training inside the dimension was flowing back to him in real time! He could feel tangible progress occurring—techniques refining, understanding deepening. It was like remembering something he’d already done, except he was experiencing it for the first time.
It’s actually working! The training transfers completely!
It was unfortunate that the clone couldn’t train his Holy energy specifically—that divine power was exclusive to his original body. He could feel the absence, like trying to grasp smoke.
But even with that limitation, this is absurdly overpowered.
Of course, he also couldn’t progress his cloning skill itself using the duplicate—that was another inherent restriction.
Even with those limitations, this capability is absolutely broken.
Leon felt forever grateful to Archon Vyrra for generously giving him that hydra core and its associated loot.
Without her intervention and gift, none of this would have been possible.
A profound realization struck him with sudden clarity, settling in his chest like a weight.
I’ve been far too passive for far too long. I haven’t been taking proper advantage of everything I possess—all these resources, abilities, opportunities.
He’d been coasting, reactive rather than proactive.
But now I must become the absolute strongest I possibly can be.
There had also been a nagging feeling lurking somewhere in his mind—anxiety about potentially leaving Seraphine far behind in terms of power progression.
But that concern is gone now. I need to be strong—strong enough to protect myself and everyone around me. That’s what matters.
Leon opened a portal to the dimensional realm in less than a second. The air shimmered and tore, revealing the familiar landscape beyond.
TEAR! OPEN! SHIMMER!

He stepped through physically with his original body, feeling the familiar shift in atmospheric pressure and temperature as he transitioned between realms. The air here was cleaner, crisper—untouched by the oppressive heat of the Pyrrhan world.
STEP! TRANSITION! ARRIVE!
He deliberately left his clone behind in the Pyrrhan realm to maintain a presence there.
Right after entering his domain, Leon immediately opened his cosmic shop interface—there was one specific item he desperately needed to purchase.
The familiar golden screen materialized before him, glowing softly in the dimensional light.
Tome of Eternal Practice (Epic – Item)
Simulates 10,000 hours of training in your mind. Usable once per day.
Price: 6,000,000 Causality
Vendor: Archivist of the Unskimmable
Leon bought it without giving the substantial cost much thought—this item had been on his priority acquisition list for quite a while.
PURCHASE! CONFIRM! DEDUCT!
Now it’s time to train seriously.
Archon Vyrra had mentioned that attacks from those rift monsters happened every single day without fail.
I have twenty-four hours of subjective time. When I emerge, I’ll be a completely different beast altogether.

The tome materialized from a glitch in reality—space folding and unfolding like origami. Leon caught it firmly, feeling its substantial weight and the rough texture of ancient leather binding against his palms. The cover was warm, almost uncomfortably so, pulsing with contained power.
SHIMMER! APPEAR! CATCH!
Time to spam every training method I possess and become as strong as I possibly can in this window.
Leon activated the Tome of Eternal Practice immediately without hesitation. The leather grew hot under his fingers, almost burning.
USE! ACTIVATE! ENGAGE!
His vision went white.
